---
title: "Radar satellite data and deep learning lower the detectability floor for low-severity spruce beetle disturbance in Southcentral Alaska"
date: today
author:
  - name: Seamus Murphy
    orcid: 0000-0002-1792-0351
abstract: |
  Spruce beetle (*Dendroctonus rufipennis*) has killed spruce across
  Southcentral Alaska since about 2016, yet roughly ninety per cent of the
  mortality sits in stands of areal severity below 0.05, beneath the detection
  floor of Landsat change analysis, and the aerial survey understates this
  dispersed damage. Few studies have asked whether the temporal dimension of
  freely available satellite data reaches below that floor, and none has asked
  it of a spruce beetle outbreak with radar, which cloud does not stop. This
  study tests whether temporal deep learning on a monthly Sentinel-1 radar
  series lowers the floor, across 160 stand blocks over the Southcentral
  outbreak region (2017 to 2026) assigned wholly to eight spatial
  cross-validation folds. Terrain-corrected dual-polarisation
  backscatter from one satellite track, speckle-filtered across the length of
  the series at 10 m on the Equi7Grid, feeds a temporal convolutional network and a Transformer
  encoder together with climate variables defined from the beetle's biology,
  trained on dead-spruce crowns digitised from statewide sub-metre mosaics of
  2020 and 2023, whose comparison gives interval-censored onset labels. Skill
  is reported per severity stratum under block cross-validation against the
  published shortwave infrared floor and evaluated against an independent
  high-resolution severity product. [Detection skill in the 0.01 to 0.10
  stratum: pending.] [Detectability floor per method: pending.] [Onset-dating
  error and the effect of interval supervision: pending.] [Contribution of
  climate variables: pending.] [Correspondence of the reconstructed outbreak
  progression with the aerial survey record: pending.] The severity strata,
  metrics and decision rules were fixed by pre-registration before outcome
  data were analysed.
keywords:

# Introduction

Recurrent outbreaks of the spruce beetle, *Dendroctonus rufipennis* (Kirby, 1837), Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae, have shaped the spruce forests of Southcentral Alaska for centuries, with outbreak extent linked to summer temperature [@Berg_2006]. From 1990 to 2000 an outbreak killed spruce across 1.19 million ha of Alaskan forest, roughly 40 per cent more than the previous 70 years together [@Werner_2006], and a new outbreak under way since about 2016 has spread from the Susitna lowlands toward the Alaska Range [@Zwieback_2024]. Where, when and how severely beetle-caused mortality occurs is foundational to hazard management, carbon accounting and understanding how a warming climate reshapes boreal disturbance [@Hicke_2024; @Patacca_2022; @Morris_2016], yet the operational damage record for Alaska rests on aerial sketch mapping, whose polygons record only what an observer saw that year and understate dispersed low-severity mortality [@Zwieback_2024].

Satellite remote sensing offers the systematic record that survey flights cannot. Four decades of Landsat observation at stand scale [@Wulder_2019], read through segmentation algorithms such as LandTrendr [@Kennedy_2010] or continuous change detection [@Zhu_2014], have produced a 25-year national record of disturbance [@White_2017] and separated defoliators from bark beetles [@Meigs_2011; @Senf_2015; @Meddens_2013], but these methods detect abrupt, stand-replacing disturbance reliably and lose skill on the partial, gradual change where insect damage lives [@Cohen_2017; @Senf_2017], so for bark beetles the mature capability is mapping the red and gray stages of heavily killed stands and low-severity dispersed mortality remains the recognised frontier [@Hicke_2024; @Marvasti_Zadeh_2023].

The size of that gap in Alaska is now quantified. @Zwieback_2024 mapped dead spruce at tree scale from 2 m WorldView-2 imagery with a convolutional network at 95 per cent average accuracy, and found that roughly 90 per cent of beetle-killed spruce in their Southcentral study area stood in stands of areal severity below 0.05, while stand-scale Landsat shortwave infrared change related clearly to severity only above 0.1, so in this mixed forest with low conifer fractions nearly all mortality sits beneath the detection floor of Landsat change analysis. High-resolution mapping closes that gap at the cost of proprietary imagery [@Hart_2015; @Nowak_2026], Alaska-wide change attribution has relied on the same survey perimeters [@Pastick_2018], occurrence models predict beetle habitat rather than damage [@Zabihi_2021], and individual-tree mortality benchmarks exist only outside Alaska [@Khatri_Chhetri_2024].

Deep learning applied to the temporal dimension offers a route below the index-based floor. One-dimensional convolutional networks [@Pelletier_2019] and self-attention models [@Ru_wurm_2020] classify satellite image time series without handcrafted temporal features [reviewed by @Miller_2024], and over the boreal forest of eastern Canada TempCNN and Transformer models on annual Landsat subsequences detected and dated partial and progressive disturbances that LandTrendr-based classification missed [@Perbet_2024]; whether that transfers from a defoliator in Quebec to a bark beetle in Alaska is unknown [@Kautz_2024]. The European literature on *Ips typographus* (Linnaeus, 1758) [@Abdullah_2018; @Huo_2021; @Dalponte_2022; @Candotti_2022] targets a tree that fades within one season, where *Dendroctonus*-attacked spruce fade over years, from green through red to gray [@Hicke_2024], so the signal here accumulates over time scales a monthly or annual series resolves, and the reference severity dataset that had been missing now exists in the tree-scale product of @Zwieback_2024, together with sub-metre statewide mosaics on which further labels can be digitised.

This study evaluates deep learning methods and a Sentinel-1 radar time series against that reference, and tests whether climate variables defined from the beetle's biology improve what the models can see. It assembles a monthly Sentinel-1 radar series over Southcentral Alaska from June 2017, trains subsequence models [after @Perbet_2024] against stand-scale severity reference data, and measures them against the published shortwave infrared floor [@Zwieback_2024]. The objectives are to (1) quantify the skill with which a Sentinel-1 radar time series estimates stand-scale areal severity of beetle-associated mortality, reported per severity stratum; (2) determine the detectability floor, the lowest severity stratum at which detection skill exceeds a pre-registered threshold, for each method; (3) estimate the year of mortality onset, supervised by onset intervals triangulated between the two label epochs, and quantify its lag relative to the reference record; (4) quantify the contribution of biologically motivated climate variables to detection skill; and (5) reconstruct the annual progression of the outbreak from its 2016 onset through the present across the Matanuska-Susitna Borough application extent, evaluating the reconstruction against the aerial survey archive.

Three hypotheses are tested over the complete outbreak trajectory. Under the null (H0), temporal deep learning models do not exceed the skill of the shortwave infrared change baseline below areal severity of 0.1, and the detection floor of @Zwieback_2024 stands; under the alternative (H1), subsequence models achieve significantly higher detection skill than the baseline within the 0.01 to 0.10 severity stratum, lowering the floor at which freely available imagery can monitor spruce beetle mortality. Under H2, models trained with mortality-onset intervals triangulated between the 2020 and 2023 label epochs date onset more accurately than the same models trained on single-epoch labels. Under H3, models receiving annual climate channels, a summer warmth index anchored on the 17 °C univoltinism threshold [@Hansen_2001], winter minimum temperature, and lagged summer means [@Berg_2006], detect low-severity mortality better than spectrally identical models without them. Estimated onset years are expected to lag true onset by one to two years, as observed for gradual disturbances elsewhere in the boreal [@Perbet_2024], and the severity strata, skill metrics and decision thresholds were fixed by pre-registration before any outcome data were analysed.

The third hypothesis rests on the beetle's biology, and its climate variables are defined from three parts of the life cycle, the generation time, the manner of spread and the winter, so the Introduction closes on them. Adult flight in Southcentral Alaska begins in early June once ambient temperature exceeds 12.8 °C [@Holsten_2001], during the rapid cambial growth of white spruce [@Hard_1985b], and whether the brood then matures in one year or two is under direct temperature control acting on the fourth larval instar and the prepupa [@Hansen_2001b], the best stand-level predictor of the univoltine proportion being cumulative hours above 17 °C from 40 to 90 days after peak flight [@Hansen_2001]. The temperature that governs it is that of the phloem rather than the air, since two-year cycles developed on the north and west faces of standing boles at a mean phloem temperature of 10.6 °C while one-year cycles developed on the south faces of the same trees at 16.5 °C [@Werner_1985]. A warm summer therefore halves the generation time without raising fecundity, and the shorter generation is what raises the rate of spruce mortality in an established outbreak [@Hansen_2003], while an obligate adult diapause requiring cold floors the life cycle at one year [@Bleiker_2019; @Davenport_2024], so the mortality a satellite series records cannot advance faster than an annual increment however warm the summer.

Spread is by threshold and by opportunity rather than along a front. Pheromone-mediated aggregation raises attack density until it suffices to kill the host [@Jenkins_2014], so mortality accumulates in foci around killed trees, and attack succeeds where host defence is overwhelmed and growth is slow, since diameter predicted susceptibility only with slower than average radial growth over the previous five years [@Hard_1983; @Hard_1985]. Populations build in windthrown and weakened hosts before erupting onto standing stands [@Reynolds_1994], and the eruption is synchronous rather than radial, at many locations at once and synchronised by regional drivers, with beetle activity correlated only within about five kilometres [@Jenkins_2014; @Hart_2017], since beetles released in Alaska were recovered at most 600 m from their overwintering sites [@Werner_1997]. The regional driver is not temperature alone, because Colorado outbreaks were predicted best by drought [@Hart_2014] and initiated in summer, winter and multi-year drought marked by low peak snow water equivalent [@Hart_2017], while cold winters held Interior Alaska populations at endemic levels until those limits eased [@Holsten_1990], so the summer temperature relationship in the Alaskan record [@Berg_2006; @Sherriff_2011] stands beside a moisture term, and a population held at endemic level erupts when the limit lifts, onto hosts already weakened.

The winter sets the last threshold, and it is a depth rather than a temperature. Larvae and adults in Alaska supercooled to about −12 °C in summer and −31 °C in winter, neither stage was freeze tolerant, and temperatures beneath the bark of standing spruce showed that only beetles hibernating below the snow line would survive a typical winter [@Miller_1987], which is why attack concentrates on the lower bole [@Hard_1985b]. Winter minimum air temperature therefore bounds survival only for brood above the snow, the snowpack that shelters the brood is the one whose low peak water equivalent marked the drought-initiated outbreaks of the Southern Rockies [@Hart_2017], and snow depth over a stand follows elevation, canopy closure and terrain, all of which the analysis grid carries, so the overwintering threshold ends as a line on the bole rather than a temperature in the air, and the climate the models received is measured from that line.

# Materials and methods

Every climate variable the models received was defined from the biology the Introduction closed on, so the climate is described first; the sections then place the outbreak in its region and in the survey record, list the inputs, describe the labels and the radar record, define what is fitted, and set out the cross-validation and the tests, with the label pipeline and the radar record recorded in full in the supplement under the same section names. All inputs were open, with scripted retrieval, checksums and a provenance manifest beside the code.

## Climate variables

Daily minimum and maximum air temperature from the Daymet version 4 gridded forcings at 1 km [@Thornton_2021], the record standing nearest to the phloem temperature and the snow depth the biology named, were reduced per 90 m stand cell and year to three variables, the summer warmth index, the cumulative degree-hours above 17 °C from June through September, a fixed-window form of the univoltinism predictor of @Hansen_2001; the winter minimum, the lowest daily minimum from November through March, the cold to which brood above the snow line is exposed [@Werner_2006; @Bentz_2010]; and the lagged summer mean, the mean summer temperature two years earlier, following the lagged association in the regional outbreak record [@Berg_2006; @Sherriff_2011].

```{r}
#| label: climate-build
#| echo: true
#| output: false
if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/climate_series.csv") ||
    max(read.csv("../02.inputs/derived/climate_series.csv")$year) < 2025) {
  library(rgee)
  ee_Initialize(project = "murphys-deforisk", quiet = TRUE)
  tpl_c <- rast("../02.inputs/zwieback-severity/merged_ref_h_c90c.tif")
  bbc <- as.vector(ext(project(as.polygons(ext(tpl_c) + 50000, crs = crs(tpl_c)), "EPSG:4326")))
  roi_c <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(bbc[1], bbc[3], bbc[2], bbc[4]))
  dm <- ee$ImageCollection("NASA/ORNL/DAYMET_V4")
  yearly <- function(y) {
    smr <- dm$filterDate(sprintf("%d-06-01", y), sprintf("%d-10-01", y))
    tmean <- smr$map(function(img)
      img$select("tmax")$add(img$select("tmin"))$divide(2)$rename("tmean"))
    gdd <- tmean$map(function(img)
      img$subtract(17)$max(0)$multiply(24))$sum()$rename("warmth")
    smean <- tmean$mean()$rename("summer_mean")
    wtr <- dm$filterDate(sprintf("%d-11-01", y - 1), sprintf("%d-04-01", y))$
      select("tmin")$min()$rename("winter_min")
    gdd$addBands(smean)$addBands(wtr)$reduceRegion(
      reducer = ee$Reducer$mean(), geometry = roi_c, scale = 1000, maxPixels = 1e10)
  }
  vals <- lapply(1990:2025, function(y) unlist(yearly(y)$getInfo()))
  clim <- data.frame(year = 1990:2025, do.call(rbind, vals))
  clim$summer_mean_lag2 <- c(NA, NA, head(clim$summer_mean, -2))
  dir.create("../02.inputs/derived", showWarnings = FALSE)
  write.csv(clim, "../02.inputs/derived/climate_series.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
clim <- read.csv("../02.inputs/derived/climate_series.csv")
```

#| label: climate-rasters
#| echo: true

dir.create("../02.inputs/climate", showWarnings = FALSE)
todo_c <- (2012:2025)[!file.exists(sprintf("../02.inputs/climate/clim_%d.tif", 2012:2025))]
if (length(todo_c)) {
  library(rgee)
  ee_Initialize(project = "murphys-deforisk", quiet = TRUE)
  tpl_c <- rast("../02.inputs/zwieback-severity/merged_ref_h_c90c.tif")
  bbc <- as.vector(ext(project(as.polygons(ext(tpl_c) + 50000, crs = crs(tpl_c)), "EPSG:4326")))
  roi_c <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(bbc[1], bbc[3], bbc[2], bbc[4]))
  dm <- ee$ImageCollection("NASA/ORNL/DAYMET_V4")
  for (y in todo_c) {
    smr <- dm$filterDate(sprintf("%d-06-01", y), sprintf("%d-10-01", y))
    tmean <- smr$map(function(img)
      img$select("tmax")$add(img$select("tmin"))$divide(2)$rename("tmean"))
    img <- tmean$map(function(im) im$subtract(17)$max(0)$multiply(24))$sum()$
      rename("warmth")$
      addBands(tmean$mean()$rename("summer_mean"))$
      addBands(dm$filterDate(sprintf("%d-11-01", y - 1), sprintf("%d-04-01", y))$
                 select("tmin")$min()$rename("winter_min"))
    url <- img$toFloat()$getDownloadURL(list(region = roi_c, scale = 1000,
                                             crs = "EPSG:32605", format = "GEO_TIFF"))
    old_to <- options(timeout = 600)
    try(download.file(url, sprintf("../02.inputs/climate/clim_%d.tif", y), mode = "wb",
                      quiet = TRUE), silent = TRUE)
    options(old_to)
  }
}

```{r}
#| label: climograph-build
#| echo: true
#| output: false
if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/climate_monthly.csv")) {
  library(rgee)
  ee_Initialize(project = "murphys-deforisk", quiet = TRUE)
  tpl_m <- rast("../02.inputs/climate/clim_2016.tif")
  bbm <- as.vector(ext(project(as.polygons(ext(tpl_m), crs = crs(tpl_m)), "EPSG:4326")))
  aoi_m <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(bbm[1], bbm[3], bbm[2], bbm[4]))
  dm <- ee$ImageCollection("NASA/ORNL/DAYMET_V4")$
    filterDate("1990-01-01", "2024-01-01")$filterBounds(aoi_m)
  rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:12, function(m) {
    sub <- dm$filter(ee$Filter$calendarRange(m, m, "month"))
    img <- sub$select(c("tmax", "tmin"))$mean()$
      addBands(sub$select("prcp")$mean()$multiply(
        c(31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31)[m])$rename("prcp_month"))
    v <- img$reduceRegion(reducer = ee$Reducer$mean(), geometry = aoi_m,
                          scale = 1000, maxPixels = 1e9, bestEffort = TRUE)$getInfo()
    data.frame(month = m, tmax = v$tmax, tmin = v$tmin, prcp = v$prcp_month)
  }))
  rows$tmean <- (rows$tmax + rows$tmin) / 2
  write.csv(rows, "../02.inputs/derived/climate_monthly.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
clim_m <- read.csv("../02.inputs/derived/climate_monthly.csv")
clim_m$month_name <- month.abb[clim_m$month]
```

@fig-climograph gives the seasonal setting, in which the warmest month, `r month.name[warm_m$month]`, had a mean daily maximum of `r sprintf("%.1f", warm_m$tmax)` °C over 1990 to 2023, below the 17 °C threshold, so degree-hours accrue only on the warmer days of the window and a summer a degree above normal shortens the generation [@Hansen_2001]; @fig-climate shows the three variables over 1990 to 2023.

```{r}
#| label: fig-climograph
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Climograph of the study area from Daymet version 4 daily forcings averaged over 1990 to 2023, monthly mean precipitation as bars against monthly mean, maximum and minimum daily air temperature. The horizontal line marks the 17 °C threshold above which spruce beetle development accrues toward a one-year generation, and the shaded band marks June through September, the window over which the summer warmth index integrates. Adult flight occurs in early summer, at the opening of that band."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.2
base <- floor(min(clim_m$tmin) / 5) * 5
sc <- max(clim_m$prcp) / (max(clim_m$tmax) - base)
ggplot(clim_m, aes(x = month)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 5.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "grey85", alpha = .55) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = month - .35, xmax = month + .35, ymin = base,
                ymax = base + prcp / sc), fill = "steelblue4", alpha = .75) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 17, linetype = "22", colour = "#C0392B") +
  annotate("text", x = 1.4, y = 18.2, label = "17 °C univoltinism threshold",
           size = 2.5, colour = "#C0392B", hjust = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmax, colour = "Daily maximum"), linewidth = .5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmean, colour = "Daily mean"), linewidth = .6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmin, colour = "Daily minimum"), linewidth = .5) +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = c("Daily maximum" = "#E67E22",
                                       "Daily mean" = "grey20",
                                       "Daily minimum" = "steelblue4")) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Temperature (°C)",
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(~ (. - base) * sc, name = "Precipitation (mm)")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb, expand = c(.01, .01)) +
  labs(x = NULL) + th + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: climate-variance
#| echo: true
#| output: false
if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/climate_variance.csv")) {
  cf <- sort(list.files("../02.inputs/climate", pattern = "^clim_[0-9]{4}[.]tif$",
                        full.names = TRUE))
  nm <- c("summer warmth index", "winter minimum", "lagged summer mean")
  cv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(b) {
    st <- rast(lapply(cf, function(x) rast(x)[[b]]))
    v <- terra::extract(st, vect(st_transform(blocks, crs(st))), fun = mean,
                        na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)
    v <- v[complete.cases(v), ]
    data.frame(channel = nm[b], blocks = nrow(v), between_year = sd(colMeans(v)),
               between_block = mean(apply(v, 2, sd)))
  }))
  cv$ratio <- cv$between_year / cv$between_block
  write.csv(cv, "../03.outputs/climate_variance.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
climvar <- read.csv("../03.outputs/climate_variance.csv")
cvr <- function(ch) climvar$ratio[climvar$channel == ch]
```

  bbm <- as.vector(ext(project(as.polygons(ext(tpl_m), crs = crs(tpl_m)), "EPSG:4326")))
  roi_m <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(bbm[1], bbm[3], bbm[2], bbm[4]))
  dm <- ee$ImageCollection("NASA/ORNL/DAYMET_V4")
  for (y in todo_m) {
    img <- ee$Image$cat(lapply(1:12, function(m) {
      d <- dm$filterDate(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", y, m), sprintf("%d-%02d-01", y + (m == 12), m %% 12 + 1))
      tmean <- d$map(function(im) im$select("tmax")$add(im$select("tmin"))$divide(2)$rename("tmean"))
      ee$Image$cat(
        d$select("tmax")$mean()$rename(sprintf("tmax_%02d", m)),
        d$select("tmin")$mean()$rename(sprintf("tmin_%02d", m)),
        tmean$map(function(im) im$subtract(17)$max(0)$multiply(24))$sum()$rename(sprintf("warmth_%02d", m)),
        d$select("prcp")$sum()$rename(sprintf("prcp_%02d", m)))
    }))
    url <- img$toFloat()$getDownloadURL(list(region = roi_m, scale = 1000,
                                             crs = "EPSG:32605", format = "GEO_TIFF"))
    old_to <- options(timeout = 600)
    download.file(url, sprintf("../02.inputs/climate/monthly/clim_m_%d.tif", y), mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
    options(old_to)
  }
}
clim_names <- c("tmax", "tmin", "warmth", "prcp")
clim_stack <- rast(lapply(2017:2025, function(y) {
  r <- rast(sprintf("../02.inputs/climate/monthly/clim_m_%d.tif", y))
  names(r) <- paste(rep(clim_names, 12), sprintf("%d-%02d-01", y, rep(1:12, each = 4)), sep = "_")
  r
}))
warmth_check <- global(abs(sum(clim_stack[[paste0("warmth_2020-", sprintf("%02d", 6:9), "-01")]]) -
                             resample(rast("../02.inputs/climate/clim_2020.tif")[[1]], clim_stack)), "max", na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(warmth_check$max < 0.01)
```

The three annual channels are what the third hypothesis names, and the amendment of 2026-09-09, approved 2026-09-10, fits climate to the model at the radar's monthly step as well, from the same daily forcings reduced per calendar month from June 2017 to December 2025, the end of the Daymet record, to the mean daily maximum, the mean daily minimum, the degree-hours above 17 °C and the precipitation total; the June to September degree-hours of the monthly series sum to the annual warmth index within `r format(signif(warmth_check$max, 1))` in every cell. Over the `r climvar$blocks[1]` sampled blocks the summer warmth index varied `r sprintf("%.2f", cvr("summer warmth index"))` times as much between years as between blocks, a timing channel, while the winter minimum and the lagged summer mean varied more between blocks within a year than between years, at `r sprintf("%.2f", cvr("winter minimum"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", cvr("lagged summer mean"))`, so two of the three carry spatial contrast the network can use; Figure S1 draws the warmth index over the blocks in the warmest and the coolest year.

## Study area

The study area was the Southcentral Alaska outbreak region, centred on the Susitna lowlands and the Matanuska-Susitna Valley and bounded by the Talkeetna Mountains and the Alaska Range. Forests are boreal mosaics of white spruce (*Picea glauca* (Moench) Voss), black spruce (*P. mariana* (Mill.) Britton et al.), Alaska birch (*Betula neoalaskana* Sarg.) and trembling aspen (*Populus tremuloides* Michx.), with wetlands and mixed stands in which conifer fractions of 10 to 30% predominate, and the outbreak reached the area around 2016 and had exhausted much of the large white spruce by 2021 [@Zwieback_2024]; the nearest precedent is the Kenai Peninsula outbreak of 1987 to 2000 [@Boucher_2006; @Roynolds_1996]. Training and cross-validation blocks lay in a 39,050 km² confirmatory window around the footprint of the independent severity reference, the Talkeetna to Byers Lake area, which was held out for evaluation, and the Matanuska-Susitna Borough was the application extent for the wall-to-wall maps. The design samples one outbreak in one region, so the maps beyond the window are application products the cross-validation does not confirm, and nothing in it estimates transfer to the Kenai Peninsula, to Interior Alaska or to another *Dendroctonus* system. Every map used WGS 84 UTM zone 5N, the grid of the severity reference, and @fig-studyarea locates the blocks and their folds over the terrain with the survey-recorded outbreak footprint.

## Outbreak history

```{r}
#| label: spread-build
#| echo: true
#| output: false
if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/survey_spread.csv")) {
  sf_use_s2(FALSE)
  pg <- st_read("../02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb", quiet = TRUE,
                query = paste("SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, ACRES, Shape FROM",
                              "DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10",
                              "WHERE DCA_COMMON_NAME LIKE '%spruce beetle%'"))
  ll <- st_coordinates(st_transform(suppressWarnings(st_centroid(st_geometry(pg))), 4326))
  sp <- data.frame(year = pg$SURVEY_YEAR, acres = pg$ACRES, lat = ll[, 2], lon = ll[, 1])
  sp <- sp[complete.cases(sp) & sp$acres > 0, ]
  sp$hectares <- sp$acres * 0.40468564
  write.csv(sp, "../03.outputs/survey_spread.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
spread <- read.csv("../03.outputs/survey_spread.csv")
spread_yr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(spread, spread$year), function(d)
  data.frame(year = d$year[1], lat = sum(d$lat * d$hectares) / sum(d$hectares),
             kha = sum(d$hectares) / 1000)))
spread_fit <- lm(lat ~ year, spread_yr)
spread_cap <- paste0(
  "Spruce beetle damage recorded by the Alaska aerial detection survey, ",
  min(spread$year), " to ", max(spread$year), ", from all ",
  format(nrow(spread), big.mark = ","), " polygons the survey attributes to the ",
  "agent with a recorded area. (a) Damage area by quarter-degree latitude band ",
  "and survey year, on a square-root colour scale so the smaller years remain ",
  "visible. (b) The area-weighted mean latitude of damage in each year, sized by ",
  "the area recorded that year, with a least-squares line and its interval. The ",
  "survey records where observers flew, so the recorded centre reflects survey ",
  "effort as well as beetle activity."
)
```

The aerial detection survey has recorded spruce beetle damage in Alaska since 1997, and @fig-spread draws its whole span. Across `r nrow(spread_yr)` survey years the area-weighted mean latitude of recorded damage moved north by `r sprintf("%.2f", coef(spread_fit)[2] * diff(range(spread_yr$year)))` degrees, about `r sprintf("%.0f", coef(spread_fit)[2] * diff(range(spread_yr$year)) * 111)` km \[F(1, `r spread_fit$df.residual`) = `r sprintf("%.2f", summary(spread_fit)$fstatistic[1])`, p = `r sprintf("%.3f", summary(spread_fit)$coefficients[2, 4])`, R² = `r sprintf("%.3f", summary(spread_fit)$r.squared)`\], a drift rather than a march, since the trend explained under a quarter of the year-to-year variance, the survey records where observers flew, and the mass at the start of the record is the Kenai Peninsula outbreak while the mass at the end is the Susitna lowlands, so the centre of recorded damage moved between two events rather than one population tracked as it moved. @fig-survey-map draws the same record on the ground.


```{r}
#| label: fig-spread
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: !expr spread_cap
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5.4
spread$band <- floor(spread$lat * 4) / 4
sp_grid <- aggregate(hectares ~ band + year, spread, sum)
ps_a <- ggplot(sp_grid, aes(year, band, fill = hectares / 1000)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt", name = "kha") +
  labs(title = "(a) Recorded damage by latitude", x = NULL,
       y = "Latitude (degrees north)") + th
ps_b <- ggplot(spread_yr, aes(year, lat)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#C0392B", fill = "#C0392B",
              alpha = .15, linewidth = .5, formula = y ~ x) +
  geom_point(aes(size = kha), colour = "steelblue4", alpha = .85) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(.8, 4.5), name = "kha") +
  labs(title = "(b) Area-weighted mean latitude", x = NULL,
       y = "Latitude (degrees north)") + th
ps_a / ps_b
```

The study drew on `r nrow(inp)` input datasets in four roles (@tbl-inputs). Reference data were the crown delineations digitised on the two State of Alaska mosaic epochs, seeded by the released labels and network of @Zwieback_2024, and that study's independent severity rasters; predictor data were the Sentinel-1 radar series; terrain and conifer fraction [@Macander_2022] conditioned sampling; and the aerial detection survey polygons and their flown-area footprints stratified the sample and separated surveyed absence from non-survey.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inputs
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Input datasets, their roles, and access terms."
fmt_tbl(inp)
```

## Training data

Stand-scale areal severity of beetle-associated dead spruce for the Talkeetna to Byers Lake area in 2021, derived by @Zwieback_2024 from a convolutional network applied to WorldView-2 imagery and therefore a model product with its own documented error rather than ground truth, was used at its three released stand scales solely for independent evaluation, and its metadata alone were inspected before pre-registration.

```{r}
#| label: severity-metadata
#| echo: true
sev <- lapply(sprintf("../02.inputs/zwieback-severity/merged_ref_h_c%sc.tif", c(30, 90, 250)), rast)
data.frame(
  file = vapply(sev, function(r) basename(sources(r)), ""),
  resolution = vapply(sev, function(r) paste(round(res(r)), collapse = " x "), ""),
  ncell = vapply(sev, ncell, numeric(1)),
  crs = vapply(sev, function(r) st_crs(crs(r))$Name, "")
)
```

## Crown labels

```{r}
#| label: label-numbers
#| echo: true
#| output: false
pairs <- read.csv("../03.outputs/label_pairs.csv")
crown_m <- read.csv("../03.outputs/crown_net_metrics.csv")
best <- crown_m[which.max(crown_m$val_iou), ]
op <- read.csv("../03.outputs/crown_operating_point.csv")
tq <- read.csv("../03.outputs/triage_queue.csv")
```

Reference labels were dead spruce crowns digitised over the 160 sampled blocks on the State of Alaska mosaics of 2020, at 0.5 m, and 2023, at 0.3 m, at which a single crown is many pixels wide; the mosaics are licensed Maxar imagery, so the pixels were processed locally and never redistributed, and the study publishes only the derived crowns and severity fractions, as @Zwieback_2024 did. Labelling ran in four stages, adapted from @Zwieback_2024 for the pre-labelling and from @Khatri_Chhetri_2024 for the triage. The released dead-spruce network of @Zwieback_2024 was adapted from its seven WorldView-2 bands to the four the mosaics carry and fine-tuned on that study's published crown delineations, `r format(sum(pairs$crowns), big.mark = ",")` crowns over `r nrow(pairs)` delineation areas, keeping the epoch that validated best on held-out areas, at a pixel recall of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$val_recall)` and precision of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$val_precision)`. Its candidates were refined into crown polygons with DeepForest [@Weinstein_2019] and the Segment Anything Model [@Wu_2023] and written per block and epoch at a probability threshold of 0.5, `r format(sum(tq$candidates), big.mark = ",")` candidate polygons at a median of `r median(tq$candidates)` per block, for two annotators to accept, edit or reject in QGIS with a third adjudicating. Accepted crowns were rasterised to the fraction of each 10 m Equi7Grid cell they cover, the areal severity, and comparing the two epochs gave each crown a state, dead by 2020, died between 2020 and 2023, or alive through 2023, which supplied the interval-censored onset labels and returned to triage any crown dead in 2020 and alive in 2023. The published labels of @Zwieback_2024 joined the training pool within their own delineation areas with cuts at 2018 and 2021, while that study's severity rasters took no part in labelling; mortality agent was inferred from context, and dead spruce hidden under closed deciduous canopy are absent from the labels. The tuning pairs, the network, the queue and the planned separability test are in the supplement.

## Stand cells

```{r}
#| label: stand-cells
#| echo: true
#| output: false
strata <- c(0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1)
strata_lab <- c("0-0.01", "0.01-0.03", "0.03-0.05", "0.05-0.10", "0.10-0.20", ">0.20")
RES <- 10; NCELL <- 76
if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/stand_cells_10m.gpkg")) {
  eq7 <- st_transform(blocks, "EPSG:27705")
  cells10 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(eq7)), function(i) {
    bb <- st_bbox(eq7[i, ])
    x0 <- round(mean(bb[c("xmin", "xmax")]) / RES) * RES - (NCELL / 2) * RES
    y1 <- round(mean(bb[c("ymin", "ymax")]) / RES) * RES + (NCELL / 2) * RES
    r <- rast(nrows = NCELL, ncols = NCELL, xmin = x0, xmax = x0 + NCELL * RES,
              ymin = y1 - NCELL * RES, ymax = y1, crs = "EPSG:27705")
    values(r) <- 1; r[c(1, NCELL), ] <- NA; r[, c(1, NCELL)] <- NA
    p <- st_as_sf(as.polygons(r, dissolve = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE))
    inside <- st_within(st_centroid(st_geometry(p)), st_geometry(eq7[i, ]), sparse = FALSE)[, 1]
    st_sf(block = eq7$block[i], fold = eq7$fold[i], geometry = st_geometry(p[inside, ]))
  }))
  cells10$id <- seq_len(nrow(cells10))
  for (epoch in c(2020, 2023)) {
    cells10[[paste0("sev_", epoch)]] <- 0
    for (b in unique(cells10$block)) {
      cr <- st_read(sprintf("../02.inputs/prelabels/%d/block_%03d.gpkg", epoch, b), quiet = TRUE)
      if (!nrow(cr)) next
      i <- which(cells10$block == b)
      a <- st_intersection(st_sf(id = i, geometry = st_geometry(cells10[i, ])),
                           st_transform(st_union(cr), "EPSG:27705"))
      area <- tapply(as.numeric(st_area(a)), a$id, sum)
      cells10[[paste0("sev_", epoch)]][as.integer(names(area))] <- area / RES^2
    }
  }
  cells10$stratum <- cut(cells10$sev_2023, strata, strata_lab, include.lowest = TRUE)
  st_write(cells10, "../02.inputs/derived/stand_cells_10m.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)
  xy <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(cells10)))
  write.csv(data.frame(st_drop_geometry(cells10), x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2]),
            "../02.inputs/derived/stand_cells_10m.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
cells10 <- read.csv("../02.inputs/derived/stand_cells_10m.csv")
cells10$stratum <- factor(cells10$stratum, strata_lab)
cell_n <- table(cells10$stratum)
cell_summary <- aggregate(cbind(cells = 1, at_or_above = sev_2023 >= 0.01) ~ block + fold, cells10, sum)
write.csv(cell_summary, "../03.outputs/stand_cells_10m_by_block.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

The sample unit was the 10 m cell of the Equi7Grid on which the radar record is held, a cell entering the sample when its centre lay inside a block and outside the outer ring of the block's window, which the speckle filter leaves empty, giving `r format(nrow(cells10), big.mark = ",")` cells over the 160 blocks. Until the annotation of the triage queue is complete the labels are the machine candidates themselves, written at a probability of 0.5, reprojected to the same grid and dissolved to the fraction of each cell they cover in each mosaic epoch, and the 2023 fraction placed each cell in one of the six pre-registered severity strata, `r format(cell_n[["0-0.01"]], big.mark = ",")` cells below 0.01 and `r format(sum(cell_n) - cell_n[["0-0.01"]], big.mark = ",")` at or above it, of which `r format(sum(cell_n[c("0.01-0.03", "0.03-0.05", "0.05-0.10")]), big.mark = ",")` sat in the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum the first hypothesis is scored in. Every result trained on these labels is therefore a result on machine labels, the seed round of the annotation design, and is reported as such.

## Survey polygons

Sketch-mapped damage polygons for Alaska, all survey years, were not used as labels, because positional accuracy is coarse, low-severity damage is under-recorded, and the intensity attribute counts faded trees per treed area, which is not commensurable with pixel-fraction severity [@Zwieback_2024]. They stratified the block sample by recorded damage history and, through the flown-area footprints, distinguished surveyed absence from non-survey; annual extent is tabulated below as descriptive context.

## Radar record

```{r}
#| label: radar-record-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
s1_scenes <- read.csv("../03.outputs/s1_rtc_scene_means.csv")
seen <- lapply(split(s1_scenes$block, s1_scenes$track), unique)
s1_blocks <- c(only_131 = length(setdiff(seen[["131"]], seen[["160"]])),
               both = length(intersect(seen[["131"]], seen[["160"]])),
               only_160 = length(setdiff(seen[["160"]], seen[["131"]])))
s1_nscene <- tapply(s1_scenes$scene_id, s1_scenes$track, function(x) length(unique(x)))
s1_first <- min(as.Date(s1_scenes$date[s1_scenes$track == 131]))
s1_floor30 <- read.csv("../03.outputs/radar_noise_floor_undamaged_10m.csv")
s1_ref <- read.csv("../03.outputs/radar_noise_floor.csv")
floor30 <- function(what, b, p)
  s1_floor30[[what]][s1_floor30$processing == p & s1_floor30$band == b]
ref_db <- function(q) s1_ref$value[s1_ref$quantity == q]
yr_floor <- function(b, p = "mt_filtered") floor30("year_to_year_median_db", b, p)
rep_floor <- function(b, p = "mt_filtered") floor30("repeatability_median_db", b, p)
removed <- function(b) 100 * (1 - yr_floor(b) / yr_floor(b, "unfiltered"))
canopy_ratio <- c(VV = ref_db("windthrow_vv_db") / yr_floor("VV"),
                  VH = ref_db("windthrow_vh_db") / yr_floor("VH"))
s1val <- read.csv("../03.outputs/s1gbm_validation.csv")
s1_cube_files <- list.files("../02.inputs/derived/s1_cube_10m",
                            pattern = "^SENTINEL-1_RTC_.*[.]tif$")
s1_cube_dates <- as.Date(unique(regmatches(
  s1_cube_files, regexpr("[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}", s1_cube_files))))
```

The predictor record was Sentinel-1 C-band radar over the 160 sampled blocks from June 2017 onward, with two polarisations, VV, sent and received vertically, and VH, received horizontally, which returns more from the canopy than from the ground. Radar passes through cloud, which is what limits optical observation in Southcentral Alaska, so a monthly step was available where the optical record supported an annual one. Scenes came from the Planetary Computer's terrain corrected collection, `sentinel-1-rtc`, in which the return is corrected for the slope and aspect of the ground [@Small_2011] so that terrain does not read as forest, at 10 m sampling; the comparison against Earth Engine's uncorrected collection is in the supplement under Radar record.

Two descending orbits, 131 and 160, crossed the blocks, and only orbit 131 entered the series, because it saw every block, `r s1_blocks[["only_131"]]` alone and `r s1_blocks[["both"]]` with orbit 160, which saw `r s1_blocks[["only_160"]]` alone; the two agreed over the shared blocks on the corrected record, measured in the supplement. The record began on `r format(s1_first, "%d %B %Y")`, because earlier scenes carry VV alone, and holds `r s1_nscene[["131"]]` scenes on orbit 131.

Each scene was reprojected once, by area-weighted average, onto the 10 m Equi7Grid North America (EPSG:27705), the continental grid the Sentinel-1 Global Backscatter Model is distributed on, so that the record crossed the boundary between UTM zones 5 and 6 without a seam and kept the instrument's 10 m sampling, its resolution being coarser; no layover and shadow mask was applied on the low relief of the Susitna lowlands, an omission the Limitations record.

The whole radar chain is the two chunks that follow, and nothing outside this document assembles or processes the record. The first reads every scene of orbit 131 from the Planetary Computer's `sentinel-1-rtc` collection through its STAC catalogue and blob store, reprojects each block's window once onto the 10 m Equi7Grid by area-weighted average, caches one array per scene and reshuffles the cache into one memory-mapped array per block, because a whole stack at 10 m is 5.6 GB on an 8 GB machine; it runs as shards when the cache is being filled and as a whole once it is. The second filters each block, composites it to calendar month and writes it as one tile of a local cube for the sits package, measuring the noise floor on the undamaged blocks as it goes.

```{python}
#| label: radar-extract
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| engine.path: /opt/local/bin/python3
import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import os
import threading
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

os.environ.update({
    "GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN": "EMPTY_DIR",
    "GDAL_HTTP_MULTIPLEX": "YES", "GDAL_HTTP_VERSION": "2",
    "VSI_CACHE": "TRUE", "VSI_CACHE_SIZE": "16777216", "GDAL_CACHEMAX": "32",
})
import numpy as np
import rasterio
import geopandas as gpd
from rasterio.crs import CRS
from rasterio.enums import Resampling
from rasterio.transform import from_origin
from rasterio.warp import reproject, transform_bounds
from rasterio.windows import Window, from_bounds

ROOT = Path("..")
BLOCKS = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "sample_blocks.gpkg"
CACHE = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_scene_cache_10m"
OUTDIR = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_blocks_10m"
STAC = "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1/search"
SAS = "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/sas/v1/token/sentinel-1-rtc"
BBOX = [-151.963, 61.52, -148.438, 63.467]
TRACK, RES, NCELL = 131, 10, 76
DST = CRS.from_epsg(27705)
_tok = {"v": None, "e": 0.0}
_lock = threading.Lock()


def token():
    with _lock:
        if time.time() < _tok["e"] - 300:
            return _tok["v"]
        with urllib.request.urlopen(SAS, timeout=60) as f:
            d = json.load(f)
        _tok["v"] = d["token"]
        exp = d.get("msft:expiry")
        _tok["e"] = (dt.datetime.fromisoformat(exp.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()
                     if exp else time.time() + 3300)
        return _tok["v"]


def scenes_on_track():
    body = {"collections": ["sentinel-1-rtc"], "bbox": BBOX,
            "datetime": "2017-06-03T00:00:00Z/2026-12-31T23:59:59Z",
            "query": {"sat:orbit_state": {"eq": "descending"},
                      "sat:relative_orbit": {"eq": TRACK}}, "limit": 500}
    out = []
    while True:
        req = urllib.request.Request(STAC, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                     headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as f:
            page = json.load(f)
        feats = page.get("features", [])
        for it in feats:
            p, a = it["properties"], it.get("assets", {})
            pols = p.get("sar:polarizations") or []
            if "VV" not in pols or "VH" not in pols or "vv" not in a or "vh" not in a:
                continue
            out.append({"id": it["id"], "date": p["datetime"][:10],
                        "vv": a["vv"]["href"], "vh": a["vh"]["href"]})
        nxt = [l for l in page.get("links", []) if l.get("rel") == "next"]
        if not nxt or not feats:
            break
        body = nxt[0].get("body") or body
        if "token" not in body:
            break
    out.sort(key=lambda r: (r["date"], r["id"]))
    return out


def block_grids():
    """A 76 by 76 window of 10 m Equi7 cells centred on each block, snapped to
    the grid, so every cell edge sits on a multiple of 10 m in EPSG:27705."""
    blocks = gpd.read_file(BLOCKS).to_crs(DST)
    grids = []
    for i, geom in enumerate(blocks.geometry):
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = geom.bounds
        cx, cy = (minx + maxx) / 2, (miny + maxy) / 2
        x0 = round(cx / RES) * RES - (NCELL // 2) * RES
        y1 = round(cy / RES) * RES + (NCELL // 2) * RES
        grids.append({"block": f"block_{i + 1:03d}", "x0": x0, "y1": y1,
                      "bounds": (x0, y1 - NCELL * RES, x0 + NCELL * RES, y1)})
    return grids


def read_one(src, g):
    """Read one block window and lay it on the 10 m Equi7 grid. The source
    window is clipped to the scene rather than read boundless, because a
    boundless read in rasterio is an order of magnitude slower over HTTP."""
    x0, ymin, x1, ymax = g["bounds"]
    sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1 = transform_bounds(DST, src.crs, x0, ymin, x1, ymax,
                                          densify_pts=21)
    pad = 2 * abs(src.transform.a)
    sw = from_bounds(sx0 - pad, sy0 - pad, sx1 + pad, sy1 + pad, src.transform)
    sw = sw.intersection(Window(0, 0, src.width, src.height)) \
        if (sw.col_off < src.width and sw.row_off < src.height and
            sw.col_off + sw.width > 0 and sw.row_off + sw.height > 0) else None
    dst = np.zeros((NCELL, NCELL), dtype="float32")
    if sw is None or sw.width < 1 or sw.height < 1:
        return dst
    sw = sw.round_offsets().round_lengths()
    arr_src = src.read(1, window=sw).astype("float32")
    reproject(source=arr_src, destination=dst,
              src_transform=src.window_transform(sw), src_crs=src.crs,
              dst_transform=from_origin(x0, ymax, RES, RES), dst_crs=DST,
              resampling=Resampling.average, src_nodata=0, dst_nodata=0)
    return dst


def one_scene(args):
    """One scene, every block, on one open handle per polarisation."""
    sc, grids = args
    for attempt in range(1, 5):
        try:
            tk = token()
            out = np.full((2, len(grids), NCELL, NCELL), np.nan, "float32")
            for bi, href in enumerate((sc["vv"], sc["vh"])):
                with rasterio.open(f"{href}?{tk}") as src:
                    for gi, g in enumerate(grids):
                        arr = read_one(src, g)
                        out[bi, gi] = np.where(arr > 0, arr, np.nan)
            final = CACHE / f"{sc['id']}.npy"
            with open(final.with_name(final.name + ".part"), "wb") as fh:
                np.save(fh, out)
            os.replace(final.with_name(final.name + ".part"), final)
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            if "403" in str(e):
                with _lock:
                    _tok["e"] = 0.0
            if attempt < 4:
                time.sleep(15 * attempt)
                continue
            print(f"  skip {sc['id']} after {attempt} attempts: {type(e).__name__}", flush=True)
            return False


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--shard", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--nshards", type=int, default=1)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUTDIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    grids = block_grids()
    scenes = scenes_on_track()
    todo = [s for i, s in enumerate(scenes)
            if i % a.nshards == a.shard and not (CACHE / f"{s['id']}.npy").exists()]
    print(f"{len(scenes)} scenes on track {TRACK}, shard {a.shard} of {a.nshards} "
          f"reads {len(todo)}, {len(grids)} blocks of {NCELL} by {NCELL} at {RES} m "
          f"on EPSG:27705", flush=True)
    t0 = time.time()
    n_fail = 0
    for i, sc in enumerate(todo):
        n_fail += not one_scene((sc, grids))
        if (i + 1) % 5 == 0:
            print(f"  shard {a.shard}: {i + 1}/{len(todo)}, {n_fail} failed, "
                  f"{time.time() - t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
    print(f"shard {a.shard} read in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s, {n_fail} failed", flush=True)
    if a.nshards > 1:
        return

    # Reshuffle the per-scene cache into one memory-mapped array per block.
    have = [s for s in scenes if (CACHE / f"{s['id']}.npy").exists()]
    missing = [s["id"] for s in scenes if s not in have]
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{len(missing)} of {len(scenes)} scenes are not in the cache, "
                           f"so the block stacks would be incomplete; rerun the shards. "
                           f"First missing: {missing[:5]}")
    n = len(have)
    mm = [np.lib.format.open_memmap(OUTDIR / f"{g['block']}.npy", mode="w+",
                                    dtype="float32", shape=(n, 2, NCELL, NCELL))
          for g in grids]
    step = 40
    for k in range(0, n, step):
        chunk = np.stack([np.load(CACHE / f"{s['id']}.npy") for s in have[k:k + step]])
        for gi in range(len(grids)):
            mm[gi][k:k + chunk.shape[0]] = chunk[:, :, gi]
        print(f"  reshuffled {min(k + step, n)}/{n}", flush=True)
    for m in mm:
        m.flush()
    np.savez(OUTDIR / "meta.npz",
             scene_id=np.array([s["id"] for s in have]),
             date=np.array([s["date"] for s in have]),
             block=np.array([g["block"] for g in grids]),
             x0=np.array([g["x0"] for g in grids], "float64"),
             y1=np.array([g["y1"] for g in grids], "float64"),
             bands=np.array(["VV", "VH"]), res_m=RES, ncell=NCELL, track=TRACK,
             crs="EPSG:27705")
    print(f"wrote {len(grids)} block stacks of ({n}, 2, {NCELL}, {NCELL}) to "
          f"{OUTDIR.name}", flush=True)


if not (OUTDIR / "meta.npz").exists():
    import sys
    sys.argv = [sys.argv[0]]
    main()
```

```{python}
#| label: radar-cube
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| engine.path: /opt/local/bin/python3
import csv
import os
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import rasterio
import geopandas as gpd
from rasterio.transform import from_origin

ROOT = Path("..")
IN = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_blocks_10m"
FLT = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_blocks_10m_mtfiltered"
CUBE = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_cube_10m"
BLOCKS = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "sample_blocks.gpkg"
FLOOR = ROOT / "03.outputs" / "radar_noise_floor_undamaged_10m.csv"
MONTHS = (6, 7, 8, 9)
W = 3


def local_mean(a, w):
    r = w // 2
    valid = np.isfinite(a)
    filled = np.where(valid, a, 0.0)
    s = np.zeros_like(filled)
    n = np.zeros(filled.shape, dtype="int16")
    for dy in range(-r, r + 1):
        for dx in range(-r, r + 1):
            s += np.roll(np.roll(filled, dy, axis=-2), dx, axis=-1)
            n += np.roll(np.roll(valid, dy, axis=-2), dx, axis=-1)
    out = np.divide(s, np.maximum(n, 1), where=n > 0)
    out[..., :r, :] = np.nan
    out[..., -r:, :] = np.nan
    out[..., :, :r] = np.nan
    out[..., :, -r:] = np.nan
    out[n == 0] = np.nan
    return out


def mt_filter(stack):
    """stack (scene, band, row, col) for one block."""
    out = np.full_like(stack, np.nan)
    for bi in range(stack.shape[1]):
        I = stack[:, bi]
        E = np.stack([local_mean(I[k], W) for k in range(I.shape[0])])
        ok = np.isfinite(I) & np.isfinite(E) & (E != 0)
        ratio = np.where(ok, I / np.where(E == 0, np.nan, E), 0.0)
        c = ok.sum(axis=0)
        mean_ratio = np.where(c > 0, ratio.sum(axis=0) / np.maximum(c, 1), np.nan)
        out[:, bi] = np.where(ok, E * mean_ratio[None, ...], np.nan)
    return out


def db(a):
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        return 10 * np.log10(a)


def floors(x, dates):
    """x (scene, row, col) in dB for one band and block; returns (rep, yr)."""
    years = np.array([int(d[:4]) for d in dates])
    months = np.array([int(d[5:7]) for d in dates])
    rep, yr = [], []
    for m in MONTHS:
        monthly = {}
        for y in sorted(set(years)):
            sel = (years == y) & (months == m)
            if sel.sum() == 0:
                continue
            a = x[sel]
            n = np.isfinite(a).sum(axis=0)
            if sel.sum() >= 2:
                sd = np.nanstd(a, axis=0, ddof=1)
                rep.append(sd[n >= 2])
            monthly[y] = np.nanmean(a, axis=0)
        if len(monthly) >= 4:
            s = np.stack([monthly[y] for y in sorted(monthly)])
            n = np.isfinite(s).sum(axis=0)
            sd = np.nanstd(s, axis=0, ddof=1)
            yr.append(sd[n >= 4])
    rep = np.concatenate(rep) if rep else np.array([])
    yr = np.concatenate(yr) if yr else np.array([])
    return rep[np.isfinite(rep)], yr[np.isfinite(yr)]


def main():
    FLT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    CUBE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    z = np.load(IN / "meta.npz", allow_pickle=False)
    dates, blocks, x0s, y1s = z["date"], z["block"], z["x0"], z["y1"]
    res, ncell = int(z["res_m"]), int(z["ncell"])
    undamaged = ~gpd.read_file(BLOCKS)["damage"].astype(bool).to_numpy()
    first, last = str(dates[0])[:7], str(dates[-1])[:7]
    y0, m0 = int(first[:4]), int(first[5:])
    y1_, m1 = int(last[:4]), int(last[5:])
    months = [f"{y}-{m:02d}" for y in range(y0, y1_ + 1) for m in range(1, 13)
              if (y, m) >= (y0, m0) and (y, m) <= (y1_, m1)]
    by_month = defaultdict(list)
    for i, d in enumerate(dates):
        by_month[str(d)[:7]].append(i)
    print(f"{len(blocks)} blocks, {len(dates)} scenes, {len(months)} months "
          f"{first} to {last}", flush=True)
    acc = {("unfiltered", b): [[], []] for b in ("VV", "VH")}
    acc.update({("mt_filtered", b): [[], []] for b in ("VV", "VH")})
    for gi, blk in enumerate(blocks):
        tile = f"B{blk[-3:]}"
        raw = np.load(IN / f"{blk}.npy", mmap_mode="r")
        fpath = FLT / f"{blk}.npy"
        if fpath.exists():
            flt = np.load(fpath, mmap_mode="r")
        else:
            flt = mt_filter(np.asarray(raw))
            with open(fpath.with_name(fpath.name + ".part"), "wb") as fh:
                np.save(fh, flt)
            os.replace(fpath.with_name(fpath.name + ".part"), fpath)
        if undamaged[gi]:
            for label, st in (("unfiltered", raw), ("mt_filtered", flt)):
                for bi, band in enumerate(("VV", "VH")):
                    rep, yr = floors(db(np.asarray(st[:, bi])), dates)
                    acc[(label, band)][0].append(rep)
                    acc[(label, band)][1].append(yr)
        tr = from_origin(x0s[gi], y1s[gi], res, res)
        prof = dict(driver="GTiff", dtype="float32", count=1, nodata=np.nan,
                    width=ncell, height=ncell, crs="EPSG:27705", transform=tr,
                    compress="deflate", predictor=2)
        for m in months:
            idx = by_month.get(m, [])
            for bi, band in enumerate(("VV", "VH")):
                path = CUBE / f"SENTINEL-1_RTC_{tile}_{band}_{m}-01.tif"
                if path.exists():
                    continue
                with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
                    comp = (np.nanmean(flt[idx, bi], axis=0) if idx
                            else np.full((ncell, ncell), np.nan, "float32"))
                part = path.with_name(path.name + ".part")
                with rasterio.open(part, "w", **prof) as dst:
                    dst.write(comp.astype("float32"), 1)
                    dst.update_tags(scenes=len(idx), month=m, res_m=res,
                                    track=int(z["track"]), filter="quegan2000_3x3",
                                    units="gamma0 linear power")
                os.replace(part, path)
        if gi % 20 == 0:
            print(f"  {blk} done", flush=True)
    rows = []
    for (label, band), (rep, yr) in acc.items():
        rep, yr = np.concatenate(rep), np.concatenate(yr)
        rows.append({"processing": label, "band": band,
                     "repeatability_median_db": round(float(np.median(rep)), 3),
                     "repeatability_n": int(rep.size),
                     "year_to_year_median_db": round(float(np.median(yr)), 3),
                     "year_to_year_q25_db": round(float(np.percentile(yr, 25)), 3),
                     "year_to_year_q75_db": round(float(np.percentile(yr, 75)), 3),
                     "year_to_year_n": int(yr.size),
                     "blocks": int(undamaged.sum()), "months": "6-9",
                     "support": "10 m cell"})
    with FLOOR.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"wrote {FLOOR.name} and the cube under {CUBE.name}", flush=True)


if not FLOOR.exists():
    main()
```

Every date was kept, because the multi-temporal speckle filter of the Sentinel-1 Toolbox after @Quegan_2000, implemented in the second chunk above, takes its noise reduction from the length of the series; speckle is the grainy noise of a radar image. Each date keeps its own local mean over a 3 by 3 window, the ratios of every image to its local mean are averaged across all dates, and each date's mean is multiplied back, so real change between dates stays while the speckle cancels across the stack, as @fig-filter shows for one block on one date.

```{python}
#| label: filter-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| engine.path: /opt/local/bin/python3
import os, csv
import numpy as np

if not os.path.exists("../03.outputs/filter_effect_block.csv"):
    z = np.load("../02.inputs/derived/s1_blocks_10m/meta.npz")
    dates, blocks, x0, y1 = z["date"], z["block"], z["x0"], z["y1"]
    di = next(i for i, d in enumerate(dates) if str(d).startswith("2019-07"))
    for k, b in enumerate(blocks):
        raw = np.load(f"../02.inputs/derived/s1_blocks_10m/{b}.npy", mmap_mode="r")[di, 0]
        if np.isfinite(raw[1:-1, 1:-1]).all():
            break
    flt = np.load(f"../02.inputs/derived/s1_blocks_10m_mtfiltered/{b}.npy", mmap_mode="r")[di, 0]
    with open("../03.outputs/filter_effect_block.csv", "w", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.writer(fh)
        w.writerow(["block", "date", "x0", "y1", "before", "after"])
        w.writerows([b, dates[di], x0[k], y1[k], r, a] for r, a in
                    zip(np.asarray(raw).ravel(), np.asarray(flt).ravel()))
```

The chain was checked against the Sentinel-1 Global Backscatter Model [@Bauer_Marschallinger_2021], an independent processor's mean backscatter of 2016 and 2017 over the same ground, and across the `r s1val$n_blocks[1]` blocks the two agreed in pattern at a correlation of `r sprintf("%.3f", s1val$pearson_r[s1val$band == "VV"])` in VV and `r sprintf("%.3f", s1val$pearson_r[s1val$band == "VH"])` in VH; their levels differ by `r sprintf("%.2f", s1val$offset_db[s1val$band == "VV"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", s1val$offset_db[s1val$band == "VH"])` dB, an offset decomposed in the supplement.

The noise floor was measured where nothing had happened, on the `r unique(s1_floor30$blocks)` blocks in which the aerial survey never recorded damage, at 10 m, June through September, after the filter, as the year-to-year spread of one cell's monthly mean for the same calendar month, which is what a multi-year change has to clear, `r sprintf("%.2f", yr_floor("VV"))` dB in VV and `r sprintf("%.2f", yr_floor("VH"))` dB in VH. Against the total canopy removal by windthrow of `r sprintf("%.2f", ref_db("windthrow_vv_db"))` dB in VV and `r sprintf("%.2f", ref_db("windthrow_vh_db"))` dB in VH [@R_etschi_2019, page 11] that floor gave ratios of `r sprintf("%.2f", canopy_ratio[["VV"]])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", canopy_ratio[["VH"]])`, so at a single 10 m cell in a single year total canopy removal sat at the floor and low-severity mortality below it. That is not the model's floor, which has not been measured, because the model reads a trajectory across many months and years rather than one difference; what the model can detect is what the pre-registered tests measure, and the floor before the filter is in the supplement.

From the filtered stack the series was composited to calendar month and written as a local cube for the sits package, `r format(length(s1_cube_files), big.mark = ",")` rasters, one per block, polarisation and month, holding VV and VH over `r length(s1_cube_dates)` months from `r format(min(s1_cube_dates), "%B %Y")` to `r format(max(s1_cube_dates), "%B %Y")`, from which the models receive the Kennaugh elements K0 and K1, the sum and the difference of the VV and VH intensities after @Hechtl_2025, formed inside sits and converted to decibels afterwards; @fig-season draws the cube's July and November of one year block by block, the seasonal cycle the Limitations return to.

## Radar samples

```{r}
#| label: radar-samples
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(sits)
s1 <- sits_cube(source = "MPC", collection = "SENTINEL-1-RTC",
                data_dir = "../02.inputs/derived/s1_cube_10m",
                parse_info = c("X1", "X2", "tile", "band", "date"))
kennaugh <- function(s) {
  s <- sits_select(s, start_date = "2017-06-01", end_date = "2025-12-01")
  s <- sits_apply(s, K0 = 10 * log10(VV + VH), K1 = 10 * log10(VV - VH))
  sits_select(s, bands = c("K0", "K1"))
}
set.seed(20260812)
positive <- cells10$sev_2023 >= 0.01
draw <- positive | seq_len(nrow(cells10)) %in% sample(which(!positive), 3 * sum(positive))
if (!file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/samples_10m_raw.rds")) {
  pts <- st_as_sf(cells10[draw, ], coords = c("x", "y"), crs = "EPSG:27705")
  pts$label <- as.character(pts$stratum)
  saveRDS(sits_get_data(s1, samples = pts[, "label"], label_attr = "label",
                        multicores = 4, progress = FALSE),
          "../02.inputs/derived/samples_10m_raw.rds")
}
n_nonfinite <- function(s) sum(vapply(s$time_series, function(ts)
  sum(!is.finite(as.matrix(ts[setdiff(names(ts), "Index")]))), integer(1)))
impute_series <- function(s) {
  s$time_series <- lapply(s$time_series, function(ts) {
    for (b in setdiff(names(ts), "Index")) if (any(!is.finite(ts[[b]]))) {
      v <- ts[[b]]; v[!is.finite(v)] <- NA
      ts[[b]] <- approx(seq_along(v), v, seq_along(v), rule = 2)$y
    }
    ts
  })
  s
}
add_climate <- function(s) {
  pts <- project(vect(cbind(s$longitude, s$latitude), crs = "EPSG:4326"), "EPSG:32605")
  cv <- terra::extract(clim_stack, pts, ID = FALSE)
  s$time_series <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(s)), function(i) {
    ts <- s$time_series[[i]]
    for (v in clim_names) ts[[toupper(v)]] <- as.numeric(cv[i, paste(v, format(ts$Index), sep = "_")])
    ts
  })
  s
}
cell_meta <- function(s, cells) {
  pts <- crds(project(vect(cbind(s$longitude, s$latitude), crs = "EPSG:4326"), "EPSG:27705"))
  i <- match(paste(round(pts[, 1]), round(pts[, 2])), paste(round(cells$x), round(cells$y)))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(i), !anyDuplicated(i))
  cells[i, c("id", "block", "fold", "sev_2020", "sev_2023", "stratum")]
}
samples10 <- kennaugh(readRDS("../02.inputs/derived/samples_10m_raw.rds"))
imputed10 <- n_nonfinite(samples10)
samples10 <- add_climate(impute_series(samples10))
meta10 <- cell_meta(samples10, cells10)
n_steps <- nrow(samples10$time_series[[1]])
```

The seed round drew every cell at or above 0.01 and three times as many cells below it at random with a fixed seed, `r format(nrow(samples10), big.mark = ",")` cells in all, and read each cell's series from its block's tile of the cube through the sits package at the cell centre, over the `r n_steps` monthly steps from June 2017 to December 2025, two calendar months of which hold no scene on orbit 131; K0 and K1 were then formed and converted to decibels, and the `r format(imputed10, big.mark = ",")` values where the difference of the two polarisations was not positive were filled by linear interpolation along the series. The four monthly climate values of the Daymet cell holding each cell were joined at every step, so that every sample carried two radar channels and four climate channels on one timeline.

## Subsequence sampling

Following @Perbet_2024, the record is cut into fixed-length subsequences, seven to ten years on the annual record as pre-registered and a span the amendment of 2026-09-09 fixes on the monthly one, with the onset date at a randomised position within each labelled window, never the first step, so the models learn the shape of the trajectory rather than a calendar position [@Iwana_2021]. Every labelled stand is observed from June 2017 through the present, so the models recognise a trajectory rather than a change from a pre-outbreak state, as @Hechtl_2025 did; each labelled cell contributes its severity fraction, its onset interval, credited anywhere within the bracket, and the climate values at the same monthly step, undisturbed stands from surveyed-absence areas complete the set, and @fig-design draws the sampling scheme and the two-head design as pre-registered.

```{r}

(a) The annual record 2014 to 2025 is cut into fixed-length subsequences of seven to ten years, four of which are drawn as examples; the onset year sits at a randomised position inside each window and never at its first year, so the network learns the shape of the trajectory rather than a calendar position. The shaded band is the censoring interval for a stand alive at the 2020 label epoch and dead by the 2023 one; a stand already dead in 2020 carries an open bracket before that epoch instead, which is the case for the first and third subsequences drawn. (b) One convolutional trunk over the temporal axis feeds two heads, severity and relative onset year, and the onset head is scored against the bracket rather than a point, which is the loss H2 is defined by."
