## Architectures

Two networks are applied on identical inputs, following @Perbet_2024. TempCNN applies one-dimensional convolutions along the time axis without pooling [@Pelletier_2019], followed by dense layers and task heads, and the Transformer encoder weights every observation of the series against every other by self-attention [@Ru_wurm_2020]. In boreal disturbance classification TempCNN matched or exceeded a LandTrendr and random forest workflow, with its largest margins on partial disturbance, and the Transformer came within two accuracy points of it [@Perbet_2024].

## Baseline model

The comparator for the first hypothesis was restated by the unsigned amendment of 2026-09-09. The pre-registered null model was the stand-scale change analysis that defines the current floor [@Zwieback_2024], pre-outbreak minus post-outbreak summer shortwave-infrared reflectance per stand cell, which cannot be formed on a record that begins after the outbreak did, so the comparator is the published floor itself, the severity of 0.1 above which @Zwieback_2024 found that change related clearly to severity, the quantity the title claims to lower; a radar change baseline needs a pre-outbreak radar state and a single-date radar classifier would test the time series rather than the floor. The annual random forest mapping of @Bright_2020, trained on high-resolution crowns aggregated to percent dead at 30 m, is the published state of the art for the task and enters as a comparator [see also @Ye_2021].

## Model training

Both networks are trained on identical inputs with two heads, a severity output classified at the pre-registered breaks with the continuous fraction kept for regression, and a relative onset output, through the sits package [@Simoes_2021] on its torch backend, with Adam, cross-entropy losses, dropout and weight decay, and hyperparameters tuned on a validation split held apart from every test block. The onset head is a discrete-time formulation over the censoring bracket after the neural survival model of @Gensheimer_2019, which scores an interval label without inventing a point within it, and the ablations for the second and third hypotheses retrain the same architecture with point onset labels in place of intervals and with the climate values removed; depths, loss weights and schedules are fixed at pre-registration, and configurations and logs are archived with the code.

## Model evaluation

Evaluation uses block spatial cross-validation, the 160 blocks assigned wholly to eight folds against leakage through spatial autocorrelation [@Perbet_2024; @Roberts_2017; @Karasiak_2021], with skill reported per severity stratum. Detection is summarised by full confusion matrices with user's and producer's accuracy per class and the spatial unit stated [@Olofsson_2014; @Stehman_2019; @Stehman_2011], without the kappa coefficient [@Foody_2020], and the primary metric is recall at a fixed precision of 0.90 in the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum, the pairing that describes a rare positive class [@Saito_2015; @Sofaer_2019]. Severity regression is summarised by root-mean-square error, relative RMSE normalised by the stratum mean of the reference severity, mean absolute error, and Theil's U inequality coefficient with its bias, variance and covariance decomposition [@Gupta_2009; @Hodson_2021], and onset dating by mean absolute error in years, all with fold-wise dispersion. Hypothesis tests are paired and fold-wise, a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on the primary metric difference with a block-bootstrap confidence interval [@Demsar_2006], supported by McNemar's test on paired cell-level detections [@Dietterich_1998]; H1 compares deep and baseline skill across folds within the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum, H2 is an ablation with single-epoch labels in place of triangulated onset intervals, compared on onset mean absolute error, H3 the equivalent ablation on inputs, climate-augmented against spectral-only models, on the primary detection metric, and the three form one Holm-corrected family. The severity product of @Zwieback_2024 provides a fully independent evaluation in the Talkeetna to Byers Lake footprint, using only fold models whose training blocks exclude it, and the reconstructed outbreak progression is evaluated by areal correspondence with annual aerial survey extent [@Perbet_2024; @Perbet_2025] and reported as descriptive.

### Evaluation harness

Every metric and test above is implemented below, before any label exists, and exercised on constructed inputs whose answers follow from their construction, with the chunk stopping if any disagrees.

```{r}
#| label: eval-harness
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Recall at a fixed precision. The operating point is chosen on the calibration
# data and applied unchanged elsewhere, per the pre-registration: choosing it on
# the test fold would report the best threshold in hindsight.
threshold_at_precision <- function(score, positive, target = 0.90) {
  ord <- order(score, decreasing = TRUE)
  tp <- cumsum(positive[ord])
  prec <- tp / seq_along(tp)
  ok <- which(prec >= target & tp > 0)
  if (!length(ok)) return(Inf)          # target precision unreachable
  score[ord][max(ok)]
}
recall_at_threshold <- function(score, positive, thr) {
  if (!sum(positive)) return(NA_real_)
  if (!is.finite(thr)) return(0)
  sum(score >= thr & positive) / sum(positive)
}

# Confusion matrix with user's accuracy (correct / predicted as that class) and
# producer's accuracy (correct / reference of that class).
confusion <- function(truth, pred, lev = sort(unique(c(truth, pred)))) {
  m <- table(pred = factor(pred, lev), truth = factor(truth, lev))
  d <- diag(m)
  data.frame(class = lev,
             n_reference = as.integer(colSums(m)),
             n_predicted = as.integer(rowSums(m)),
             users = ifelse(rowSums(m) > 0, d / rowSums(m), NA_real_),
             producers = ifelse(colSums(m) > 0, d / colSums(m), NA_real_),
             row.names = NULL)
}

rmse <- function(obs, pred) sqrt(mean((pred - obs)^2))
mae <- function(obs, pred) mean(abs(pred - obs))
rrmse <- function(obs, pred) rmse(obs, pred) / mean(obs)

# Theil's U inequality coefficient with the bias, variance and covariance
# proportions of mean squared error, which sum to one by construction. The
# decomposition separates systematic offset from unexplained scatter.
theil <- function(obs, pred) {
  mse <- mean((pred - obs)^2)
  if (mse == 0) return(c(U = 0, bias = 0, variance = 0, covariance = 0))
  n <- length(obs)
  sd_p <- sqrt(mean((pred - mean(pred))^2))     # population sd, so the
  sd_o <- sqrt(mean((obs - mean(obs))^2))       # proportions sum to one
  r <- if (sd_p == 0 || sd_o == 0) 0 else cor(obs, pred)
  c(U = sqrt(mse) / (sqrt(mean(obs^2)) + sqrt(mean(pred^2))),
    bias = (mean(pred) - mean(obs))^2 / mse,
    variance = (sd_p - sd_o)^2 / mse,
    covariance = 2 * (1 - r) * sd_p * sd_o / mse)
}

# Paired fold-wise test: one-sided Wilcoxon signed rank on the per-fold
# difference, with a block bootstrap over folds for the interval. Resampling
# folds rather than cells is what keeps spatial dependence inside a resampling
# unit.
paired_fold_test <- function(diff, alternative = "greater", B = 10000,
                             seed = 20260812) {
  p <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(diff, alternative = alternative)$p.value)
  set.seed(seed)
  bs <- replicate(B, mean(sample(diff, length(diff), replace = TRUE)))
  c(mean_diff = mean(diff), p_value = p,
    ci_low = unname(quantile(bs, 0.025)),
    ci_high = unname(quantile(bs, 0.975)))
}

# McNemar on paired cell-level detections: only the discordant pairs carry
# information about which method is better.
mcnemar_paired <- function(correct_a, correct_b) {
  b <- sum(correct_a & !correct_b); c_ <- sum(!correct_a & correct_b)
  if (b + c_ == 0) return(c(b = 0, c = 0, p_value = 1))
  c(b = b, c = c_,
    p_value = suppressWarnings(
      mcnemar.test(matrix(c(sum(correct_a & correct_b), b, c_,
                            sum(!correct_a & !correct_b)), 2))$p.value))
}

# The detectability floor: the lowest severity stratum whose skill clears the
# pre-registered threshold. Strata must be supplied in ascending order.
detectability_floor <- function(stratum, skill, threshold = 0.50) {
  ok <- which(!is.na(skill) & skill >= threshold)
  if (!length(ok)) return(NA_character_)
  as.character(stratum[min(ok)])
}

# The three confirmatory tests form one family; Holm controls it.
holm_family <- function(p, labels) {
  data.frame(test = labels, p_raw = p,
             p_holm = p.adjust(p, method = "holm"), row.names = NULL)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: eval-checks-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
chk <- function(what, expected, got, tol = 1e-8)
  data.frame(check = what, expected = round(expected, 4),
             got = round(got, 4), passes = abs(expected - got) < tol)

# Perfectly separable scores: the 0.90-precision threshold recovers every
# positive, so recall is exactly 1.
s1 <- 10:1; p1 <- c(rep(TRUE, 5), rep(FALSE, 5))
r1 <- recall_at_threshold(s1, p1, threshold_at_precision(s1, p1, 0.90))

# Inverted scores: precision peaks at 0.5, never reaches 0.90, so the operating
# point does not exist and recall must be 0 rather than an accidental number.
p2 <- c(rep(FALSE, 5), rep(TRUE, 5))
r2 <- recall_at_threshold(s1, p2, threshold_at_precision(s1, p2, 0.90))

# A constant offset of 1: RMSE and MAE are 1, and relative RMSE is 1 / mean(obs).
o3 <- c(1, 2, 3); p3 <- o3 + 1

# Theil proportions sum to one for any non-degenerate pair, and U is 0 when
# prediction is exact.
t4 <- theil(c(0.1, 0.4, 0.2, 0.8), c(0.2, 0.3, 0.25, 0.9))
t5 <- theil(o3, o3)

# Pure bias: prediction is observation plus a constant, so all of the mean
# squared error is the bias term and none of it is variance or covariance.
t6 <- theil(o3, p3)

# Eight positive fold differences: the one-sided signed-rank p is 2^-8.
d7 <- seq(0.1, 0.8, by = 0.1)
w7 <- paired_fold_test(d7)

# Holm is never anti-conservative.
h8 <- holm_family(c(0.01, 0.02, 0.03), c("H1", "H2", "H3"))

# Skill clears 0.50 first in the third stratum.
f9 <- detectability_floor(c("0.01", "0.03", "0.05", "0.10"),
                          c(0.10, 0.20, 0.55, 0.70))

# A confusion matrix with one known error: class a is predicted for one true b,
# so user's accuracy for a is 2/3 and producer's accuracy for b is 1/2.
c10 <- confusion(c("a", "a", "b", "b"), c("a", "a", "a", "b"))

checks <- rbind(
  chk("recall at 0.90 precision, separable", 1, r1),
  chk("recall when 0.90 precision unreachable", 0, r2),
  chk("RMSE of a unit offset", 1, rmse(o3, p3)),
  chk("MAE of a unit offset", 1, mae(o3, p3)),
  chk("relative RMSE, mean 2", 0.5, rrmse(o3, p3)),
  chk("Theil proportions sum to one", 1, sum(t4[c("bias", "variance",
                                                  "covariance")])),
  chk("Theil U of an exact prediction", 0, t5[["U"]]),
  chk("pure offset is all bias", 1, t6[["bias"]]),
  chk("pure offset has no variance term", 0, t6[["variance"]]),
  chk("one-sided Wilcoxon on 8 positives", 2^-8, w7[["p_value"]], 1e-6),
  chk("bootstrap interval brackets the mean", 1,
      as.numeric(w7[["ci_low"]] <= mean(d7) && w7[["ci_high"]] >= mean(d7))),
  chk("Holm is not anti-conservative", 1,
      as.numeric(all(h8$p_holm >= h8$p_raw))),
  chk("detectability floor is the lowest clearing stratum", 0.05,
      as.numeric(f9)),
  chk("user's accuracy for class a", 2 / 3, c10$users[c10$class == "a"]),
  chk("producer's accuracy for class b", 0.5,
      c10$producers[c10$class == "b"]))

stopifnot(all(checks$passes))
```

All `r nrow(checks)` checks listed in Table S5 pass, which is the only reason the document renders past this point; two encode decisions rather than arithmetic, that the harness returns zero recall when no threshold reaches the required precision, and that the bootstrap resamples folds rather than cells, so spatial dependence stays inside the resampling unit.

## Seed training

```{r}
#| label: train-tempcnn
#| echo: true
#| output: false
arms <- list(radar = c("K0", "K1"), climate = c("K0", "K1", toupper(clim_names)))
probs_of <- function(p) do.call(rbind, lapply(p$predicted, function(x)
  as.matrix(x[, setdiff(names(x), c("from", "to", "class"))])))
run_arm <- function(s, meta, support, arm, over, under) {
  out <- sprintf("../03.outputs/fold_predictions_%s_%s.csv", support, arm)
  if (file.exists(out)) return(invisible(NULL))
  s <- sits_select(s, bands = arms[[arm]])
  s$polygon_id <- NULL
  dir.create("../02.inputs/derived/models", showWarnings = FALSE)
  rows <- list(); thr <- list()
  for (f in 1:8) {
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    tr <- s[meta$fold != f, ]; te <- s[meta$fold == f, ]
    trb <- sits_reduce_imbalance(tr, n_samples_over = over, n_samples_under = under, multicores = 2)
    trb <- trb[!vapply(trb$time_series, function(ts) anyNA(as.matrix(ts[-1])), TRUE), ]
    m <- sits_train(trb, sits_tempcnn(seed = 20260812, verbose = FALSE))
    luz::luz_save(sits_model_export(m),
                  sprintf("../02.inputs/derived/models/tempcnn_%s_%s_fold%d.pt", support, arm, f))
    p_tr <- probs_of(sits_classify(tr, m, multicores = 2, progress = FALSE))
    p_te <- probs_of(sits_classify(te, m, multicores = 2, progress = FALSE))
    mt <- meta[meta$fold != f, ]
    in_stratum <- mt$sev_2023 < 0.10
    t90 <- threshold_at_precision(1 - p_tr[in_stratum, "below"], mt$sev_2023[in_stratum] >= 0.01)
    thr[[f]] <- data.frame(support = support, arm = arm, fold = f, n_train = nrow(tr),
                           n_train_balanced = nrow(trb), n_test = nrow(te), thr90 = t90,
                           seconds = round(as.numeric(Sys.time() - t0, units = "secs")))
    rows[[f]] <- data.frame(support = support, arm = arm, fold = f, meta[meta$fold == f, names(meta) != "fold"],
                            score = 1 - p_te[, "below"], p_te, check.names = FALSE)
    write.csv(do.call(rbind, thr), sprintf("../03.outputs/fold_thresholds_%s_%s.csv", support, arm), row.names = FALSE)
  }
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, rows), out, row.names = FALSE)
}
samples10$label <- ifelse(meta10$sev_2023 >= 0.01, "at_or_above", "below")
for (arm in names(arms)) run_arm(samples10, meta10, "10m", arm, over = 2000, under = 4000)
fold_log <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list.files("../03.outputs", "^fold_thresholds_", full.names = TRUE), read.csv))
```

The seed round trained the pre-registered TempCNN through the sits package, its defaults as verified against @Pelletier_2019, three convolutional layers of 64 filters with kernel 3, dropout 0.2, a dense layer of 256 and early stopping on a fifth of the training samples held out, with a fixed seed. The machine labels support a detection head alone, since the six strata are filled very unevenly by candidates written at one probability, so the seed model was trained on the binary label at the pre-registered detection threshold, and the six-stratum head and the onset head, whose custom method follows, wait for annotated labels. Each sample entered as its full record of `r n_steps` monthly steps rather than as randomised subsequences, which the custom method below carries, and within each training set the majority class was reduced by self-organising map clustering and the minority class enlarged by synthetic interpolation, both through sits; the operating point for recall at 0.90 precision was chosen on the training folds' own predictions and applied unchanged to the held-out fold, as pre-registered. Each arm was trained eight times, once per fold, on radar alone and on radar with the four monthly climate channels, `r nrow(fold_log)` trainings taking `r round(sum(fold_log$seconds) / 60)` minutes in all on the eight gigabyte machine the study was run on.

```{r}
#| label: two-head-method
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# The pre-registered two-head model as a custom sits method, written on the
# pattern of sits_tempcnn(): the same convolutional trunk, a severity head over
# the six strata and an onset head over the monthly steps, scored against the
# censoring bracket by the marginal likelihood over the months it spans. Not
# yet run; it waits for annotated onset brackets and for review.
sits_tempcnn_twohead <- function(samples = NULL, onset_lo, onset_hi, w_onset = 1,
                                 epochs = 150L, batch_size = 64L, seed = 20260812) {
  train_fun <- function(samples) {
    labels <- sort(unique(samples$label)); code <- seq_along(labels); names(code) <- labels
    x <- sits:::.pred_features(sits:::.predictors(samples))
    n_times <- nrow(samples$time_series[[1]]); n_bands <- ncol(x) / n_times
    x <- array(as.matrix(x), c(nrow(samples), n_times, n_bands))
    y_sev <- unname(code[samples$label])
    torch::torch_manual_seed(seed)
    net <- torch::nn_module(
      initialize = function() {
        self$trunk <- torch::nn_sequential(
          torch::nn_conv1d(n_bands, 64, 3, padding = 1), torch::nn_batch_norm1d(64), torch::nn_relu(), torch::nn_dropout(0.2),
          torch::nn_conv1d(64, 64, 3, padding = 1), torch::nn_batch_norm1d(64), torch::nn_relu(), torch::nn_dropout(0.2),
          torch::nn_conv1d(64, 64, 3, padding = 1), torch::nn_batch_norm1d(64), torch::nn_relu(), torch::nn_dropout(0.2),
          torch::nn_flatten(), torch::nn_linear(64 * n_times, 256), torch::nn_batch_norm1d(256), torch::nn_relu(), torch::nn_dropout(0.5))
        self$severity <- torch::nn_linear(256, length(labels))
        self$onset <- torch::nn_linear(256, n_times)
      },
      forward = function(x) {
        h <- self$trunk(torch::torch_transpose(x, 2, 3))
        list(severity = self$severity(h), onset = self$onset(h))
      })
    loss_fn <- function(out, y) {
      # y: list(sev, lo, hi); the onset head gives a distribution over months
      # and the bracket's likelihood is the probability mass between lo and hi,
      # so a prediction anywhere inside the bracket is credited in full.
      ce <- torch::nnf_cross_entropy(out$severity, y$sev)
      logp <- torch::nnf_log_softmax(out$onset, dim = 2)
      mask <- (torch::torch_arange(1, n_times)$unsqueeze(1) >= y$lo$unsqueeze(2)) &
              (torch::torch_arange(1, n_times)$unsqueeze(1) <= y$hi$unsqueeze(2))
      ll <- torch::torch_logsumexp(logp$masked_fill(!mask, -Inf), dim = 2)
      ce - w_onset * ll$mean()
    }
    model <- net()
    opt <- torch::optim_adamw(model$parameters, lr = 5e-4, weight_decay = 1e-6)
    ds <- torch::tensor_dataset(x = torch::torch_tensor(x), sev = torch::torch_tensor(y_sev, dtype = torch::torch_long()),
                                lo = torch::torch_tensor(onset_lo, dtype = torch::torch_long()),
                                hi = torch::torch_tensor(onset_hi, dtype = torch::torch_long()))
    dl <- torch::dataloader(ds, batch_size = batch_size, shuffle = TRUE)
    for (e in seq_len(epochs)) coro::loop(for (b in dl) {
      opt$zero_grad(); l <- loss_fn(model(b$x), b); l$backward(); opt$step() })
    predict_fun <- function(values) {
      model$eval()
      v <- torch::torch_tensor(array(as.matrix(values), c(nrow(values), n_times, n_bands)))
      out <- model(v)
      p <- torch::as_array(torch::nnf_softmax(out$severity, 2)); colnames(p) <- labels
      attr(p, "onset") <- torch::as_array(torch::nnf_softmax(out$onset, 2))
      p
    }
    sits:::.set_class(predict_fun, "torch_model", "sits_model", class(predict_fun))
  }
  sits:::.factory_function(samples, train_fun)
}
```

## Generative artificial intelligence


# Results

The seed round, the TempCNN trained on the machine crown candidates over the 160 blocks between June 2017 and December 2025, is reported in the detection and climate tables below as what it is, a result on machine labels that fixes the pipeline and chooses what is annotated next, and not the confirmatory test of any hypothesis. The severity and onset tables remain shells, because both need the six-stratum and onset heads that annotated labels alone can train, and every cell in them displays as pending. Each subsection states the decision rule its table is read against, all of them fixed by pre-registration, so the reading was committed before the numbers arrived rather than fitted to them.

## Severity skill

@tbl-severity reports severity-estimation skill per severity stratum for the two deep learning models and the SWIR change baseline on identical stand cells, read down the strata rather than across the models, because the question is where skill fails rather than which model wins, and giving root-mean-square error, relative RMSE normalised by the stratum mean of the reference severity, mean absolute error, and Theil's U with its bias, variance and covariance proportions.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-severity
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Severity estimation error per severity stratum and model, from block spatial cross-validation. Values pending execution of the pre-registered analysis."
strata_lab <- c("0-0.01", "0.01-0.03", "0.03-0.05", "0.05-0.10",
                "0.10-0.20", ">0.20")
models <- c("TempCNN", "Transformer")
sev_shell <- expand.grid(Stratum = strata_lab, Model = models,
                         KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)
sev_shell[c("RMSE", "rRMSE", "MAE", "U_Theil", "U_bias", "U_var", "U_cov")] <- "pending"
fmt_tbl(sev_shell, right = c("RMSE","rRMSE","MAE","U_Theil","U_bias","U_var","U_cov"))
```

## Detection skill

```{r}
#| label: detection-skill
#| echo: true
#| output: false
fold_skill <- function(support, arm) {
  p <- read.csv(sprintf("../03.outputs/fold_predictions_%s_%s.csv", support, arm), check.names = FALSE)
  th <- read.csv(sprintf("../03.outputs/fold_thresholds_%s_%s.csv", support, arm))
  p$thr <- th$thr90[match(p$fold, th$fold)]
  p$det <- p$score >= p$thr
  p$stratum <- factor(p$stratum, strata_lab)
  by_stratum <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(p, list(p$fold, p$stratum), drop = TRUE), function(d)
    data.frame(fold = d$fold[1], stratum = d$stratum[1], n = nrow(d), detected = mean(d$det))))
  h1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(p, p$fold), function(d) {
    d <- d[d$sev_2023 < 0.10, ]
    pos <- d$sev_2023 >= 0.01
    data.frame(fold = d$fold[1], n = nrow(d), n_pos = sum(pos),
               recall90 = recall_at_threshold(d$score, pos, d$thr[1]),
               precision = if (sum(d$det)) sum(d$det & pos) / sum(d$det) else NA_real_,
               auc = if (sum(pos) && sum(!pos))
                 mean(outer(d$score[pos], d$score[!pos], ">") + 0.5 * outer(d$score[pos], d$score[!pos], "==")) else NA_real_)
  }))
  list(strata = cbind(support = support, arm = arm, by_stratum),
       h1 = cbind(support = support, arm = arm, h1))
}
runs <- expand.grid(support = "10m", arm = c("radar", "climate"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
skill <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(runs)), function(i) fold_skill(runs$support[i], runs$arm[i]))
skill_strata <- do.call(rbind, lapply(skill, `[[`, "strata"))
skill_h1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(skill, `[[`, "h1"))
det_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(skill_strata, list(skill_strata$support, skill_strata$arm, skill_strata$stratum), drop = TRUE), function(d)
  data.frame(Support = d$support[1], Channels = d$arm[1], Stratum = d$stratum[1], n = sum(d$n),
             folds = nrow(d), Detected = round(weighted.mean(d$detected, d$n), 2),
             Detected_sd = round(sd(d$detected), 2))))
det_tab <- det_tab[order(det_tab$Support, det_tab$Channels, det_tab$Stratum), ]
h1_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(skill_h1, list(skill_h1$support, skill_h1$arm), drop = TRUE), function(d)
  data.frame(support = d$support[1], arm = d$arm[1], n_pos = sum(d$n_pos),
             recall90 = mean(d$recall90, na.rm = TRUE), recall90_sd = sd(d$recall90, na.rm = TRUE),
             precision = mean(d$precision, na.rm = TRUE), auc = mean(d$auc, na.rm = TRUE))))
floors <- sapply(split(det_tab, list(det_tab$Support, det_tab$Channels), drop = TRUE), function(d)
  detectability_floor(d$Stratum[d$Stratum != "0-0.01"], d$Detected[d$Stratum != "0-0.01"]))
h1v <- function(support, arm, what) h1_tab[[what]][h1_tab$support == support & h1_tab$arm == arm]
prec_txt <- function(support, arm) if (is.na(h1v(support, arm, "precision")))
  "no held-out cell reaching the operating point" else
  sprintf("an achieved precision of %.2f on the held-out folds, against the 0.90 the operating point was chosen for", h1v(support, arm, "precision"))
floor_txt <- function(key) if (is.na(floors[[key]])) "no stratum" else paste("the", floors[[key]], "stratum")
```

@tbl-detection reports the seed round's detection per stratum, the share of each stratum's cells flagged at the operating point chosen on the training folds for 0.90 precision, with fold-wise dispersion; the detectability floor of a method is read from it as the lowest stratum whose recall reaches 0.50, a rule and a threshold both fixed before any outcome was seen, so the floor is located rather than chosen. On the `r format(h1v("10m", "radar", "n_pos"), big.mark = ",")` machine-labelled positives of the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum, the radar-only model recovered a recall of `r sprintf("%.2f", h1v("10m", "radar", "recall90"))` (fold-wise standard deviation `r sprintf("%.2f", h1v("10m", "radar", "recall90_sd"))`) with `r prec_txt("10m", "radar")`, and ranked positives above negatives with a mean fold-wise area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", h1v("10m", "radar", "auc"))`. The floor on machine labels therefore stood at `r floor_txt("10m.radar")` for the radar-only model. Table S6 will carry the H1 test on annotated labels, the fold-wise paired difference in the primary metric against the published floor within the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum, its block-bootstrap confidence interval, the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank statistic, and the McNemar cell-level check.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-detection
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Seed-round detection per severity stratum on machine labels, for the TempCNN on radar alone and on radar with monthly climate, at 10 m on the Equi7Grid. Detected is the share of the stratum's cells flagged at the operating point chosen on the training folds for 0.90 precision, so in the 0-0.01 stratum it is the false alarm rate and in every other stratum the recall, pooled over the eight folds, with the fold-wise standard deviation."
fmt_tbl(det_tab[, c("Support", "Channels", "Stratum", "n", "Detected", "Detected_sd")],
        right = c("n", "Detected", "Detected_sd"))
```

## Onset dating

@tbl-onset reports onset-year error under the two supervision regimes, testing H2, and gives mean absolute error and root-mean-square error in years, the share of predictions falling within the label bracket, and the fold-wise paired difference between triangulated and single-epoch supervision. The share falling inside the bracket is the more informative column, because mean absolute error against a bracketed truth penalises a prediction that is correct in every sense the labels can express.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-onset
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Onset-year estimation error by model and supervision regime (triangulated two-epoch intervals against single-epoch labels), with the H2 paired test. Values pending execution of the pre-registered analysis."
onset_shell <- expand.grid(Model = c("TempCNN", "Transformer"),
                           Supervision = c("Triangulated", "Single-epoch"),
                           KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)
onset_shell[c("MAE_yr", "RMSE_yr", "In_bracket", "Delta_MAE", "Wilcoxon_p")] <- "pending"
fmt_tbl(onset_shell, right = c("MAE_yr","RMSE_yr","In_bracket","Delta_MAE","Wilcoxon_p"))
```

## Climate contribution

```{r}
#| label: climate-contribution
#| echo: true
#| output: false
h3_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply("10m", function(sp) {
  a <- skill_h1[skill_h1$support == sp & skill_h1$arm == "climate", ]
  b <- skill_h1[skill_h1$support == sp & skill_h1$arm == "radar", ]
  d <- a$recall90[match(1:8, a$fold)] - b$recall90[match(1:8, b$fold)]
  t <- paired_fold_test(d[!is.na(d)])
  data.frame(Support = sp, Folds = sum(!is.na(d)), Delta_R90 = sprintf("%+.3f", t[["mean_diff"]]),
             CI95 = sprintf("%+.3f to %+.3f", t[["ci_low"]], t[["ci_high"]]),
             Wilcoxon_p = sprintf("%.3f", t[["p_value"]]))
}))
```

@tbl-climate reports the seed round's counterpart of H3, the fold-wise paired difference in recall at the operating point between the model given the four monthly climate channels and the model given radar alone, the pairing carrying the comparison because the two arms differ in their input channels alone and were trained on identical folds, so a difference cannot be attributed to the split. Adding climate moved recall in the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum by `r h3_tab$Delta_R90[1]` (95 per cent confidence interval `r h3_tab$CI95[1]`, p = `r h3_tab$Wilcoxon_p[1]`). The confirmatory H3 is tested on the three annual channels and annotated labels, and its p-value enters the Holm-corrected family of three with H1 and H2, each read at its corrected level rather than at 0.05.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-climate
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Seed-round comparison of the climate-augmented against the radar-only TempCNN on machine labels, the fold-wise paired difference in recall at the 0.90-precision operating point within the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum, climate minus radar, with its block-bootstrap 95 per cent confidence interval over folds and the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value. The confirmatory H3 test on the annual channels and annotated labels is not this table."
fmt_tbl(h3_tab, right = c("Folds", "Delta_R90", "CI95", "Wilcoxon_p"))
```

## Independent evaluation

Table S7 reports agreement with the untouched severity reference of @Zwieback_2024 in the Talkeetna to Byers Lake footprint, using only fold models whose training excluded the footprint, and carries the same error slate as @tbl-severity at 10 m support, alongside the published within-study errors of the reference itself for context, which are not directly comparable and are marked as such.

## Outbreak progression

Table S8 compares reconstructed annual outbreak area against the aerial survey record, reported as descriptive correspondence, giving mapped area, surveyed area, their ratio, and the intersection-over-union of the footprints per year.

# Discussion

## Detection floor

[Pending: interpretation of @tbl-severity, @tbl-detection and Table S6.] The decisive comparison is confined to the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum, where @Zwieback_2024 found stand-scale shortwave infrared change uninformative and where roughly ninety per cent of the region's beetle-killed spruce resides. If Table S6 shows the radar models clearing the published floor within that stratum, the detectability floor of freely available imagery drops below 0.1 and the fraction of the outbreak visible to open-data monitoring rises accordingly; if it does not, the result consolidates the case that sub-metre imagery is a hard requirement for low-severity beetle mapping in mixed boreal forest, already implied by the resolution comparison @Hart_2015 ran on this beetle. Either outcome resolves the transfer question left open between the defoliator system of @Perbet_2024 and the bark beetle system here, whose multi-year fade [@Hicke_2024; @Kautz_2024] presents a slower but weaker annual signal.

## Temporal supervision

[Pending: interpretation of @tbl-onset.] The triangulation design tests a claim with reach beyond this outbreak, that a second high-resolution label epoch buys more onset-dating skill than any refinement of a single-epoch label set, because it converts static labels into interval-censored ones and exposes annotation errors through cross-epoch consistency. The expected one to two year lag between spectral change and onset [@Perbet_2024] bounded what an annual optical method could date, the monthly radar record makes the censoring bracket finer without changing the loss, and @tbl-onset quantifies how much of that bound the interval supervision recovers; dating from daily commercial imagery narrows the bound at a price this study is designed to avoid [@Nowak_2026], so the comparison that matters is against what freely available data alone can date.

## Limitations

Seven limitations are known by design. First, crown labels derive from visual interpretation of sub-metre imagery, so dead spruce occluded under closed deciduous canopy are absent from training and reference data, and severity is a minimum estimate in dense mixed stands [@Zwieback_2024]. Second, the dual-polarisation radar record begins in June 2017, after the outbreak began, so there is no pre-outbreak radar state, and stands that died before the record opened carry an open bracket rather than an onset. Third, the frozen season moves C-band backscatter further than any canopy loss does, since freezing took more than 3 dB out of the ERS-1 return from a black spruce stand near Manley Hot Springs [@Rignot_1994] where total canopy removal by windthrow moved the mean by 0.45 dB in VV and 0.68 dB in VH [@R_etschi_2019], so the monthly series carries a seasonal cycle larger than its signal and the models must either work within season or learn the freeze state, which no standard for boreal forest radar specifies. Fourth, no layover and shadow mask was applied to the radar record, and thermal noise removal has not been verified; the offset against the independent mosaic being larger in the weaker polarisation is consistent with residual noise and is a hypothesis with a stated test rather than a finding. Fifth, the independent severity reference is itself a model product with documented error, so agreement with it bounds rather than establishes map accuracy. Sixth, mortality agent is inferred from context, so other agents of spruce death are conflated with beetle kill at unknown but presumed low rates [@Meigs_2011; @Senf_2015]. Seventh, the study area is one outbreak in one region, transfer to the Kenai Peninsula, to Interior Alaska or to other *Dendroctonus* systems is untested and should not be presumed [@Kautz_2024], and the outbreak studied most closely in a comparable system was governed by drought indexed by low peak snow water equivalent, which the three temperature channels used here do not carry [@Hart_2017].

## Operational implications

\[Pending: contingent on Tables S10 and S12.\] The aerial detection survey remains the only annual statewide observation system, and nothing here replaces it; the question is what a free satellite complement adds. A model whose floor sits below 0.1 severity would flag dispersed mortality the surveys under-record, at monthly cadence, through cloud, over unflown terrain, for the cost of compute alone, with Table S8 indicating how faithfully such a system would have tracked this outbreak from 2016. The label pipeline is the transferable asset, since statewide sub-metre mosaics now recur and each new epoch extends the interval-censored label set without fieldwork, which is the argument the survey programme reviews reach from the opposite direction [@Hall_2016; @Housman_2018] and the direction insect disturbance records have taken elsewhere [@White_2017; @Perbet_2025].

# Conclusion

\[Pending: quantitative sentences follow the pre-registered analysis.\] This study asks a bounded question, how much of a spruce beetle outbreak freely available satellite data can see. Prior work fixed the answer at severities above 0.1 [@Zwieback_2024], leaving most beetle-killed trees in this landscape invisible to open-data monitoring, while the wider literature on bark beetle detection has concentrated on the earliest and the most severe stages rather than on the dispersed middle [@Marvasti_Zadeh_2023; @Morris_2016]. The design tests whether temporal deep learning moves that boundary using only freely available data, a terrain-corrected Sentinel-1 radar series, crown labels digitised on public statewide mosaics, onset intervals triangulated between mosaic epochs, and an independent published severity product as referee, and whatever the direction of the result it delivers an openly reproducible record of the 2016 to 2025 Southcentral Alaska outbreak at stand scale, a labelled dataset that grows with each mosaic epoch, and a pre-registered benchmark for later methods, sensors and regions.

## Climate variables

Figure S1 shows the summer warmth index over the sampled blocks in the warmest and the coolest year of the raster record, which is what a timing channel looks like on the ground.

## Literature search

The corpus this study was argued against was assembled by a search run on 2026-09-08 over OpenAlex and arXiv, with every retained record verified against Crossref by content negotiation on its digital object identifier before it entered the bibliography. Six strands were searched. Five took their keywords from the title, namely spruce beetle with remote sensing, deep learning over satellite image time series, low-severity and partial disturbance detection, bark beetle mortality mapping, and boreal Alaskan forest disturbance, each restricted to 2010 and later. The sixth, on harmonisation between the Operational Land Imager and the MultiSpectral Instrument, was added on 2026-09-08 after the optical record, since set aside, showed a reflectance step at its sensor boundary, so that strand answered a question the data raised rather than one the title anticipated. Records were retained where they reported a method for detecting or mapping insect-caused tree mortality from satellite or airborne imagery, supplied a deep learning architecture for satellite image time series, or reported spruce beetle outbreak ecology bearing on the climate mechanism tested here; records reporting agriculture, fire, land cover, tundra or carbon cycle work were excluded, as were sensor descriptions carrying no detection method. The screening table is committed with the manuscript at `02.inputs/derived/literature_screening.csv`, one row per record with its strand, its decision and the reason for that decision, and the counts in the main text are read from it at render time.

## Crown labels

Reference labels were produced by machine-assisted digitisation of dead spruce crowns on the statewide sub-metre mosaics, acquired in 2020 at 0.5 m and in 2023 at 0.3 m resolution, over sample blocks stratified by conifer fraction and survey-recorded damage history. Imagery was obtained as four-band chips from the USDA NRCS image services, whose export endpoint carries the same mosaics. The route is public but the pixels are not, since the service records the Alaska Vivid imagery as a dataset licensed from Maxar to USDA-FPAC in 2020, with copyright retained by the vendor. Imagery was therefore processed locally and never redistributed, and what this study publishes from it are the derived crown delineations and stand-level severity fractions, not the pixels, on the same footing as the published delineations of @Zwieback_2024, which were drawn on proprietary imagery that their release could not include. Label preparation ran in four stages.

1.  **Pre-labelling.** The released dead-spruce network of @Zwieback_2024 was the only domain-tuned component available, but it could not be applied to these mosaics as released. It was trained on seven pansharpened WorldView-2 bands, blue, green, yellow, red, red edge and two near-infrared bands, and its encoder's first layer was widened from three channels to seven to match; the four-band mosaics used here supply no yellow, red-edge or second near-infrared channel. The network was therefore adapted rather than applied. The first-layer weights for the four channels the two sensors share were retained, the remaining three discarded, and the network fine-tuned on the published crown labels of the same study, which were rasterised against mosaic imagery over their own delineation areas. Those areas, not the sample blocks, supplied the tuning imagery, because the delineations intersect only four blocks and all four fall in the held-out reference fold.
2.  **Crown segmentation.** Candidate detections were refined into crown polygons with general-purpose segmentation models, DeepForest crown detection [@Weinstein_2019] supplying box prompts to the Segment Anything Model (SAM2) through the segment-geospatial toolchain [@Wu_2023], an established zero-shot pipeline for tree delineation. Segmentation ran on the project's cloud GPU; outputs were vector crown candidates scored by the dead-spruce probability.
3.  **Cleaning and triage.** Candidates below a minimum crown area or outside plausible crown geometry were dropped; overlapping detections were merged. Two annotators then accept, edit or reject each candidate independently in QGIS, with a third adjudicating disagreements [after @Khatri_Chhetri_2024]. Fully occluded dead spruce under closed deciduous canopy remain undetectable in RGB imagery and are an acknowledged limitation carried forward from @Zwieback_2024.
4.  **Aggregation, triangulation and classification.** Mortality agent was inferred from context throughout, since no crown was confirmed by ground observation, so other agents of spruce death enter the labels as beetle kill at a rate this design cannot measure. Accepted crowns were rasterised to stand-cell areal severity fractions at 30 and 90 m, and each labelled stand was classified as low, medium or high disturbance at the pre-registered severity breaks. Cross-epoch triangulation then assigned every crown a temporal state, either dead by 2020, died between 2020 and 2023, or alive through 2023, yielding interval-censored onset labels for the dating head, verified pre-mortality trajectories for exploratory green-stage analysis, and confirmed-alive negatives. The same comparison cleaned the labels, since a crown dead in 2020 must remain dead in 2023, and violations were returned to triage, a consistency check unavailable to single-epoch designs.

The published crown labels of @Zwieback_2024, distributed under an attribution licence, additionally enter the training pool within their delineation areas, contributing temporal cuts at their image dates of 2018 and 2021. Combined with the 2020 and 2023 mosaic epochs, four temporal cuts are available in the Talkeetna to Byers Lake area, narrowing onset brackets there to one to two years. The severity rasters of @Zwieback_2024, by contrast, take no part in label preparation; they remain the untouched independent evaluation dataset described under Model evaluation.

Tuning pairs were assembled below. For each delineation area holding crowns, a four-band chip at the 2020 mosaic resolution and the matching crown mask rasterised from the published polygons. The crowns were delineated on imagery of August 2021, one year after the 2020 mosaic, so a crown that died during that year was marked dead over imagery in which it was still living. This is label noise of known sign, and it is one-directional, in that it can only teach the network that living crowns are dead, never the reverse. Its size was bounded by the fraction of crowns dying in that single year and was reported with the pairs. One delivered file declares a geographic coordinate reference system while holding UTM zone 5N coordinates, which makes a crown's computed area billions of square metres if taken at face value, so it is relabelled without transforming. A failed download is written to the table as such rather than skipped, so a fetch that failed cannot read as an area that never held crowns.

```{r}
#| label: label-training-pairs
#| echo: true
#| output: false
lab_f <- list.files("../02.inputs/zwieback-labels/gpkg", pattern = "_labels[.]gpkg$",
                    full.names = TRUE)
dir.create("../02.inputs/label-pairs", showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/label_pairs.csv")) {
  rows <- list()
  options(timeout = 300)
  for (f in lab_f) {
    l <- suppressWarnings(st_read(f, quiet = TRUE))
    if (nrow(l) == 0) next
    id <- sub("_labels[.]gpkg$", "", basename(f))
    if (!identical(st_crs(l)$epsg, 32605L) &&
        suppressWarnings(st_bbox(l))[["xmin"]] > 1000)
      l <- st_set_crs(l, 32605)
    bb <- st_bbox(l)
    px <- round(c(bb["xmax"] - bb["xmin"], bb["ymax"] - bb["ymin"]) / 0.5)
    img_f <- sprintf("../02.inputs/label-pairs/%s_img.tif", id)
    msk_f <- sprintf("../02.inputs/label-pairs/%s_mask.tif", id)
    if (!file.exists(img_f)) {
      u <- sprintf(paste0(
        "https://apps.geo.fpac.usda.gov/nrcs-imagery/rest/services/",
        "ortho_imagery/alaska_vivid_2020_50cm/ImageServer/exportImage?",
        "bbox=%f,%f,%f,%f&bboxSR=32605&imageSR=32605&size=%d,%d",
        "&format=tiff&f=image"),
        bb["xmin"], bb["ymin"], bb["xmax"], bb["ymax"], px[1], px[2])
      ok <- FALSE
      for (attempt in 1:3) {
        ok <- !inherits(try(download.file(u, img_f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE),
                            silent = TRUE), "try-error")
        if (ok && inherits(try(rast(img_f), silent = TRUE), "try-error")) {
          unlink(img_f)
          ok <- FALSE
        }
        if (ok) break
        Sys.sleep(2)
      }
      if (!ok) {
        rows[[id]] <- data.frame(area = id, crowns = nrow(l),
                                 chip_px = "FETCH FAILED", bands = NA_integer_,
                                 crown_area_m2 = round(sum(as.numeric(st_area(l)))),
                                 pct_crown = NA_real_)
        next
      }
      Sys.sleep(0.5)
    }
    img <- rast(img_f)
    if (!file.exists(msk_f)) {
      m <- rasterize(vect(l), rast(img[[1]]), field = 1, background = 0)
      writeRaster(m, msk_f, overwrite = TRUE, datatype = "INT1U")
    }
    m <- rast(msk_f)
    rows[[id]] <- data.frame(
      area = id, crowns = nrow(l),
      chip_px = sprintf("%d x %d", ncol(img), nrow(img)), bands = nlyr(img),
      crown_area_m2 = round(sum(as.numeric(st_area(l)))),
      pct_crown = round(100 * global(m, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1], 2))
  }
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, rows), "../03.outputs/label_pairs.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
pairs <- read.csv("../03.outputs/label_pairs.csv")
```

The tuning pairs are listed in Table S1. Of `r nrow(pairs)` delineation areas holding crowns, `r sum(!is.na(pairs$bands))` yielded imagery, carrying `r format(sum(pairs$crowns[!is.na(pairs$bands)]), big.mark = ",")` of the `r format(sum(pairs$crowns), big.mark = ",")` published crowns over `r format(sum(pairs$crown_area_m2[!is.na(pairs$bands)]), big.mark = ",")` m² of delineated dead canopy; dead crowns occupy `r sprintf("%.1f%%", mean(pairs$pct_crown, na.rm = TRUE))` of chip pixels on average. That imbalance is the reason the parent study weighted the dead class twenty times the background class, and the same weighting carries over here. Two properties of the delivered labels are worth recording, since neither was documented with them. One area declared a geographic coordinate reference system while holding projected coordinates, which inflates its computed crown areas by nine orders of magnitude if taken at face value, and the delineation areas vary in size by more than two orders of magnitude, so the smallest carry too few pixels to serve as training chips and are padded at the tiling stage.

```{r}

#| echo: true
fmt_tbl(rbind(head(pairs[order(-pairs$crowns), ], 8),
              data.frame(area = sprintf("all %d areas", nrow(pairs)),
                         crowns = sum(pairs$crowns), chip_px = "",
                         bands = NA,
                         crown_area_m2 = sum(pairs$crown_area_m2),
                         pct_crown = round(mean(pairs$pct_crown), 2))),
        right = c("crowns", "bands", "crown_area_m2", "pct_crown"),
        caption = "Table S1. Tuning pairs assembled from the published crown delineations, four-band mosaic imagery at 0.5 m with the crown mask rasterised to the same grid, one pair per delineation area holding crowns. Percent crown is the share of chip pixels falling inside a delineated dead crown, which is the class balance the fine-tuning must contend with.")
```

## Crown network

The released network was adapted to the four bands these mosaics carry and fine-tuned on the tuning pairs above. Its first convolution was widened by @Zwieback_2024 from three channels to seven to match pansharpened WorldView-2, in the band order blue, green, yellow, red, red edge, near infrared-1 and near infrared-2. The mosaics here are blue, green, red and near infrared, an ordering confirmed from the imagery rather than assumed. The fourth band reached a 95th percentile far above the visible bands with a floor near zero over water and shadow, which is near-infrared behaviour, and among the visible bands the third was least correlated with it, which is red under chlorophyll absorption. The four matching input filters were therefore copied from the released weights and the three with no counterpart discarded, so tuning started from learned dead-spruce features rather than from noise. Dead crowns occupy a small minority of pixels, so the loss weighted that class twenty to one following the parent study. Areas were split by area, never by tile, so no crop of a validation area was ever seen in training. Tiles were indexed rather than held in memory, because holding every crop costs about 580 MB on top of a session already holding the study's other inputs, which drives this 8 GB machine into swap. Areas smaller than one tile were padded rather than discarded, since discarding them cost 8 of 37 areas and about a fifth of the delineated crowns. Flips, rotations and photometric jitter followed the parent study. A final batch of one tile was dropped in any epoch whose tile count was odd, because the network's pooling branch reduces a single tile to one value that batch normalisation cannot normalise in training mode, which is how the chunk ran at 72 tiles and crashed at 79. The checkpoint was kept on intersection over union rather than on either half of it, because recall alone is maximised by flagging everything and precision alone by flagging nothing, and metrics were written every epoch so a later failure could not discard earlier ones.

The chunk below runs as its own process rather than through reticulate. The manuscript has already loaded sits, which loads the R binding to libtorch, and initialising Python's torch in the same process loads a second copy of that library and segfaults the session. Running the interpreter as a subprocess keeps the two apart, and the interpreter was named explicitly because the environment's default resolves to a build that carries no torch.

```{python}
#| label: crown-finetune
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| engine.path: /opt/local/bin/python3
import os, glob, csv, numpy as np, rasterio, torch, torch.nn as nn

TILE, STRIDE, EPOCHS, DEAD_W, KEEP = 512, 384, 8, 20.0, [0, 1, 3, 5]

def index_of(area):
    with rasterio.open("../02.inputs/label-pairs/" + area + "_img.tif") as s:
        h, w = s.height, s.width
    if h < TILE or w < TILE:
        return [(area, 0, 0)]
    return [(area, y, x)
            for y in range(0, h - TILE + 1, STRIDE)
            for x in range(0, w - TILE + 1, STRIDE)]

def load(item, augment=False):
    area, y, x = item
    win = rasterio.windows.Window(x, y, TILE, TILE)
    with rasterio.open("../02.inputs/label-pairs/" + area + "_img.tif") as s:
        img = s.read(window=win).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
    with rasterio.open("../02.inputs/label-pairs/" + area + "_mask.tif") as s:
        msk = s.read(1, window=win).astype(np.int64)
    if img.shape[1] < TILE or img.shape[2] < TILE:
        py, px = TILE - img.shape[1], TILE - img.shape[2]
        img = np.pad(img, ((0, 0), (0, py), (0, px)), mode="symmetric")
        msk = np.pad(msk, ((0, py), (0, px)), mode="symmetric")
    if augment:
        if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
            img, msk = img[:, :, ::-1], msk[:, ::-1]
        if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
            img, msk = img[:, ::-1, :], msk[::-1, :]
        if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
            k = int(np.random.randint(1, 4))
            img, msk = np.rot90(img, k, (1, 2)), np.rot90(msk, k, (0, 1))
        img = np.clip(img * np.random.uniform(0.9, 1.1)
                      + np.random.uniform(-0.05, 0.05), 0, 1)
    return np.ascontiguousarray(img), np.ascontiguousarray(msk)

torch.manual_seed(20260812)
areas = sorted(os.path.basename(f)[:-8]
               for f in glob.glob("../02.inputs/label-pairs/*_img.tif"))
val_areas = set(areas[::5])
trn_areas = [a for a in areas if a not in val_areas]
trn = [t for a in trn_areas for t in index_of(a)]
val = [t for a in sorted(val_areas) for t in index_of(a)]
dev = torch.device("mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")

def build_net():
    net = torch.load("../02.inputs/zwieback-cnn/model.p", map_location="cpu",
                     weights_only=False)
    old = net.backbone.conv1
    new = nn.Conv2d(4, old.out_channels, old.kernel_size, old.stride,
                    old.padding, bias=False)
    with torch.no_grad():
        new.weight.copy_(old.weight[:, KEEP, :, :])
    net.backbone.conv1 = new
    net.aux_classifier = None
    return net.to(dev)

if not (os.path.exists("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt")
        and os.path.exists("../03.outputs/crown_net_metrics.csv")):
    net = build_net().train()
    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(
        weight=torch.tensor([1.0, DEAD_W], device=dev))
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(net.parameters(), lr=1e-4)
    rows, best_iou = [], -1.0
    for ep in range(EPOCHS):
        net.train()
        order = torch.randperm(len(trn)).tolist()
        tot = 0.0
        for i in range(0, len(order), 2):
            b = [load(trn[j], augment=True) for j in order[i:i+2]]
            if len(b) < 2:
                continue
            x = torch.tensor(np.stack([t[0] for t in b])).to(dev)
            y = torch.tensor(np.stack([t[1] for t in b])).to(dev)
            opt.zero_grad()
            l = loss_fn(net(x)["out"], y)
            l.backward(); opt.step()
            tot += float(l.detach()) * len(b)
        net.eval()
        tp = fp = fn = 0
        with torch.no_grad():
            for item in val:
                img, msk = load(item)
                x = torch.tensor(img[None]).to(dev)
                p = net(x)["out"].argmax(1)[0].cpu().numpy()
                tp += int(((p == 1) & (msk == 1)).sum())
                fp += int(((p == 1) & (msk == 0)).sum())
                fn += int(((p == 0) & (msk == 1)).sum())
        prec = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0
        rec = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0
        iou = tp / (tp + fp + fn) if tp + fp + fn else 0.0
        saved = iou > best_iou
        if saved:
            best_iou = iou
            torch.save(net.state_dict(), "../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt")
        rows.append(dict(epoch=ep + 1, train_loss=round(tot / len(trn), 4),
                         val_precision=round(prec, 3), val_recall=round(rec, 3),
                         val_iou=round(iou, 3), checkpointed=saved,
                         n_train_tiles=len(trn), n_val_tiles=len(val),
                         n_train_areas=len(trn_areas), n_val_areas=len(val_areas)))
        with open("../03.outputs/crown_net_metrics.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
            w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
            w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)

if (os.path.exists("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt")
        and not os.path.exists("../03.outputs/crown_operating_point.csv")):
    import rasterio.features
    from shapely.geometry import shape
    net = build_net()
    net.load_state_dict(torch.load("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt",
                                   map_location=dev))
    net.eval()
    GSD, MIN_CROWN_M2 = 0.5, 1.0
    sweep = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        probs = []
        for item in val:
            img, msk = load(item)
            p = torch.softmax(net(torch.tensor(img[None]).to(dev))["out"], 1)
            probs.append((p[0, 1].cpu().numpy(), msk))
    for thr in [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9]:
        n_cand = n_hit = n_true = n_reached = 0
        cand_area = scored_area = 0.0
        for pr, msk in probs:
            binmask = (pr >= thr).astype(np.uint8)
            polys = [(shape(g), v) for g, v in
                     rasterio.features.shapes(binmask, mask=binmask == 1)]
            keep = [g for g, _ in polys if g.area * GSD * GSD >= MIN_CROWN_M2]
            truth = [shape(g) for g, v in
                     rasterio.features.shapes(msk.astype(np.uint8),
                                              mask=msk.astype(np.uint8) == 1)]
            n_cand += len(keep); n_true += len(truth)
            n_hit += sum(1 for g in keep if any(g.intersects(t) for t in truth))
            n_reached += sum(1 for t in truth if any(g.intersects(t)
                                                     for g in keep))
            cand_area += sum(g.area for g in keep) * GSD * GSD
            scored_area += msk.size * GSD * GSD
        sweep.append(dict(threshold=thr, candidates=n_cand,
                          candidates_hitting_a_crown=n_hit,
                          reference_crowns=n_true,
                          crowns_reached=n_reached,
                          polygon_precision=round(n_hit / n_cand, 3) if n_cand else 0.0,
                          crown_recall=round(n_reached / n_true, 3) if n_true else 0.0,
                          crowns_per_candidate=round(n_reached / n_cand, 1)
                          if n_cand else 0.0,
                          area_flagged=round(cand_area / scored_area, 3)
                          if scored_area else 0.0,
                          candidates_per_km2=round(
                              n_cand / (len(val) * (TILE * GSD) ** 2 / 1e6), 1)))
    with open("../03.outputs/crown_operating_point.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(sweep[0]))
        w.writeheader(); w.writerows(sweep)
```

Per-epoch figures are in Table S2. Tuning used `r crown_m$n_train_tiles[1]` crops from `r crown_m$n_train_areas[1]` areas against `r crown_m$n_val_tiles[1]` crops from `r crown_m$n_val_areas[1]` held-out areas. The retained network is the one that validates best, epoch `r best$epoch` of `r max(crown_m$epoch)` trained, at a recall of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$val_recall)` and a precision of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$val_precision)`. `r if (best$epoch == max(crown_m$epoch)) "Validation intersection over union was still rising when the schedule ended, so the length of the run bounds the network rather than the network having converged." else "Validation intersection over union falls after that epoch while the training loss keeps falling, so the schedule already runs past its useful length."` For a pre-labeller feeding human triage the operating direction is nonetheless deliberate, because an annotator rejects a false candidate in one action, whereas a crown the network never proposes is never reviewed, and the twenty-to-one class weighting is what buys that recall. These are pixel-wise figures, so the precision an annotator experiences depends on candidate polygons after cleaning rather than on this number directly.

The operating point was chosen on polygon counts after the minimum-area filter, on held-out areas only, because an annotator accepts or rejects candidate polygons rather than pixels. Crowns reached was counted alongside candidates that hit one, because raising the threshold erodes a blob covering several crowns into one piece per crown, which raises the count of candidates hitting a crown without reaching a single crown the lower threshold missed, and without the second count that erosion reads as a gain in precision. The sweep ran down to 0.1 because crown recall was still rising at the lowest threshold first measured.

```{r}
#| label: block-area
#| echo: true
#| output: false
blk_km2 <- sum(as.numeric(st_area(blocks))) / 1e6
```

The full sweep is in Table S3. The queue was generated at the threshold that keeps candidates per square kilometre within what one annotator can work through, not at the threshold that maximises any statistic. The counts above convert directly, since the `r nrow(blocks)` blocks cover `r sprintf("%.1f", blk_km2)` km² per mosaic epoch, so a rate of `r sprintf("%.0f", op$candidates_per_km2[op$threshold == 0.5])` candidates per square kilometre at a probability threshold of 0.5 implies roughly `r format(round(op$candidates_per_km2[op$threshold == 0.5] * blk_km2), big.mark = ",")` candidates per epoch to review. Polygon precision and crown recall move in opposite directions across the sweep, precision from `r sprintf("%.2f", op$polygon_precision[op$threshold == 0.3])` at a threshold of 0.3 to `r sprintf("%.2f", op$polygon_precision[op$threshold == 0.7])` at 0.7 while the share of delineated crowns reached by any candidate falls from `r sprintf("%.2f", op$crown_recall[op$threshold == 0.3])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", op$crown_recall[op$threshold == 0.7])`, because a higher threshold erodes one candidate covering many crowns into one candidate per crown rather than reaching crowns the lower threshold missed. Precision read alone therefore rewards the threshold that finds fewest crowns. Crown recall keeps rising as the threshold falls, to `r sprintf("%.2f", op$crown_recall[op$threshold == 0.1])` at 0.1, but a candidate stops being one crown well before that, holding `r sprintf("%.1f", op$crowns_per_candidate[op$threshold == 0.1])` crowns at 0.1 and `r sprintf("%.1f", op$crowns_per_candidate[op$threshold == 0.5])` at 0.5, and flagging `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * op$area_flagged[op$threshold == 0.1])` per cent of the scored area against `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * op$area_flagged[op$threshold == 0.5])` per cent. A candidate an annotator accepts or rejects in one action has to be one crown, so the usable range ends near 0.3, where recall is `r sprintf("%.2f", op$crown_recall[op$threshold == 0.3])` and each candidate holds `r sprintf("%.1f", op$crowns_per_candidate[op$threshold == 0.3])` crowns. At that point four crowns in ten are never proposed for review, which is a limit of the network rather than of the threshold, and it bounds what the pre-labeller can save an annotator. Figure S2 draws both, since the tuning trajectory and the operating point are the two things the annotation plan rests on.

Precision, recall and intersection over union are pixel-wise against the published delineations, which are themselves imperfect targets over 2020 imagery, since a crown that died between the mosaic and the 2021 delineation is marked dead over imagery in which it was still living, so measured precision is a lower bound.")

## Triage queue

The queue is summarised by epoch in Table S4. Candidates were written per block and per epoch as GeoPackage layers that open directly in QGIS, each polygon carrying its mean dead-spruce probability and its area, so triage can be ordered by confidence rather than by position. The 2023 mosaic was resampled to the 2020 ground sample distance before inference, because the network was tuned at 0.5 m and its filters encode that scale. Inference was resumable, in that a block already written was skipped, so an interrupted run continued rather than restarting. The table was built from every block on disk rather than from the blocks one run wrote, because a resumed run skips everything already present and a table collected from new blocks alone undercounted silently; the numbered glob also excludes the sidecar files the external volume leaves beside each GeoPackage, which would otherwise double every count.

```{python}
#| label: triage-queue
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| engine.path: /opt/local/bin/python3
import os, csv, glob, numpy as np, rasterio, rasterio.features, torch
import torch.nn as nn, geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import shape

TILE, GSD, THR, MIN_CROWN_M2, KEEP = 512, 0.5, 0.5, 1.0, [0, 1, 3, 5]

if (os.path.exists("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt")
        and not os.path.exists("../03.outputs/triage_queue.csv")):
    net = torch.load("../02.inputs/zwieback-cnn/model.p", map_location="cpu",
                     weights_only=False)
    old = net.backbone.conv1
    new = nn.Conv2d(4, old.out_channels, old.kernel_size, old.stride,
                    old.padding, bias=False)
    with torch.no_grad():
        new.weight.copy_(old.weight[:, KEEP, :, :])
    net.backbone.conv1 = new
    net.aux_classifier = None
    dev = torch.device("mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")
    net.load_state_dict(torch.load("../02.inputs/crown_net_4band.pt",
                                   map_location=dev))
    net = net.to(dev).eval()

    for epoch in ("2020", "2023"):
        os.makedirs("../02.inputs/prelabels/" + epoch, exist_ok=True)
        for f in sorted(glob.glob("../02.inputs/chips/" + epoch + "/block_*.tif")):
            bid = os.path.basename(f)[6:9]
            gpkg = "../02.inputs/prelabels/%s/block_%s.gpkg" % (epoch, bid)
            if os.path.exists(gpkg):
                continue
            with rasterio.open(f) as s:
                img = s.read().astype(np.float32) / 255.0
                tr, crs = s.transform, s.crs
                scale = abs(tr.a) / GSD
            if abs(scale - 1) > 0.01:
                import rasterio.warp
                nh, nw = int(img.shape[1] / scale), int(img.shape[2] / scale)
                idx = (np.linspace(0, img.shape[1] - 1, nh).astype(int),
                       np.linspace(0, img.shape[2] - 1, nw).astype(int))
                img = img[:, idx[0][:, None], idx[1][None, :]]
                tr = rasterio.Affine(GSD, tr.b, tr.c, tr.d, -GSD, tr.f)
            _, h, w = img.shape
            prob = np.zeros((h, w), np.float32)
            with torch.no_grad():
                for y in range(0, max(h - TILE, 0) + 1, TILE):
                    for x in range(0, max(w - TILE, 0) + 1, TILE):
                        t = img[:, y:y+TILE, x:x+TILE]
                        py, px = TILE - t.shape[1], TILE - t.shape[2]
                        if py or px:
                            t = np.pad(t, ((0, 0), (0, py), (0, px)), "symmetric")
                        p = torch.softmax(
                            net(torch.tensor(t[None]).to(dev))["out"], 1)
                        pm = p[0, 1].cpu().numpy()
                        prob[y:y+TILE, x:x+TILE] = pm[:TILE-py or TILE,
                                                      :TILE-px or TILE]
            binmask = (prob >= THR).astype(np.uint8)
            geoms, probs, areas = [], [], []
            for g, v in rasterio.features.shapes(binmask, mask=binmask == 1,
                                                 transform=tr):
                poly = shape(g)
                if poly.area < MIN_CROWN_M2:
                    continue
                geoms.append(poly); areas.append(poly.area)
                mask = rasterio.features.geometry_mask(
                    [g], (h, w), tr, invert=True)
                probs.append(float(prob[mask].mean()))
            gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                dict(p_dead=probs, area_m2=areas, source_epoch=epoch),
                geometry=geoms, crs=crs)
            gdf.to_file(gpkg, driver="GPKG")

    rows = []
    for epoch in ("2020", "2023"):
        for f in sorted(glob.glob("../02.inputs/prelabels/" + epoch +
                                  "/block_[0-9][0-9][0-9].gpkg")):
            g = gpd.read_file(f)
            rows.append(dict(
                epoch=epoch, block=os.path.basename(f)[6:9], candidates=len(g),
                median_p=round(float(g["p_dead"].median()), 3) if len(g) else 0.0,
                median_area_m2=round(float(g["area_m2"].median()), 1)
                if len(g) else 0.0))
    if rows:
        with open("../03.outputs/triage_queue.csv", "w", newline="") as fh:
            w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
            w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)
```

That figure, not the crown-density extrapolation used for planning, is what the annotation scope decision should rest on. ## Spectral separability

Before any label enters training, the spectral basis of the visual classes is to be tested on the mosaic imagery itself. From the accepted delineations, samples of dead spruce crowns, live conifer crowns and non-forest background are drawn per epoch, and class separability in the available mosaic bands quantified by pairwise Jeffries-Matusita distance and transformed divergence, with values above 1.9 on the Jeffries-Matusita scale of 0 to 2 taken as strong separability. A principal component analysis of the same samples summarises the band space, so that component loadings identify which bands carry the dead-crown contrast, and class scores on the first two components are inspected for overlap. Classes that fail separability in an epoch are flagged, and their labels weighted or excluded at the pre-registered decision rule. The assessment runs when label digitisation begins; the code below is inert until then.

```{r}
#| label: planned-separability
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
jm <- function(a, b) {
  ma <- colMeans(a); mb <- colMeans(b)
  Sa <- cov(a); Sb <- cov(b); S <- (Sa + Sb) / 2
  B <- t(ma - mb) %*% solve(S) %*% (ma - mb) / 8 +
    log(det(S) / sqrt(det(Sa) * det(Sb))) / 2
  2 * (1 - exp(-B))
}
sep <- lapply(split(chips, chips$epoch), function(e) {
  cl <- split(e[bands_rgb], e$class)
  outer(names(cl), names(cl), Vectorize(function(i, j) jm(cl[[i]], cl[[j]])))
})
pca <- prcomp(chips[bands_rgb], scale. = TRUE)
```

## Radar record

Four choices defined the radar record, the archive, the track, the cell and the speckle treatment, and each replaced an earlier choice that was measured and found wanting. The main text gives each choice; the measurements that decided the archive and the track, the unfiltered floor the first extraction arrived at, and the check of the whole chain against an independent mosaic are recorded here. The decision to build on radar rather than on the optical composites is recorded with the measurements that forced it in `05.tasks/2026-09-09-sensor-design-decision.md`.

```{r}
#| label: radar-archive-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
s1_month <- read.csv("../03.outputs/s1_rtc_monthly.csv")
s1_inv <- read.csv("../03.outputs/mpc_s1_inventory.csv")
key <- paste(s1_month$block, s1_month$year, s1_month$month)
k0_db <- 10 * log10(s1_month$K0)
on131 <- s1_month$track == 131
on160 <- s1_month$track == 160
paired <- intersect(key[on131], key[on160])
track_diff <- k0_db[on131][match(paired, key[on131])] -
  k0_db[on160][match(paired, key[on160])]
s1_track <- c(n = length(track_diff), mean = mean(track_diff), sd = sd(track_diff))
s1_archive <- tapply(s1_inv$scenes, s1_inv$collection, sum)
s1_rtc_cost <- 100 * (s1_archive[["sentinel-1-grd"]] - s1_archive[["sentinel-1-rtc"]]) /
  s1_archive[["sentinel-1-grd"]]
```

The archive was the Planetary Computer's radiometrically terrain corrected collection, `sentinel-1-rtc`, rather than Earth Engine's `COPERNICUS/S1_GRD`, where the first extraction had been made. The collection's own description recorded its processing, the Ground Range Detected product converted to calibrated intensity by the European Space Agency's algorithm, then radiometrically terrain corrected by the flattening gamma method of @Small_2011 with PlanetDEM as the elevation source, and it is delivered as gamma nought in linear power at 10 m sampling. The Earth Engine collection was sigma nought with no terrain flattening. Compared on one acquisition over the blocks both hold, the flattened product ran above the unflattened one in both polarisations by an offset that was constant across most blocks and varied with the terrain across the rest, so the part that does not cancel between blocks follows the ground rather than the forest, which is what the correction exists to remove. The Planetary Computer had been assumed to hold fewer scenes than Earth Engine over this site, which was the reason the first extraction was built there, and the assumption was wrong. Counted through the archive's own catalogue by `05.scripts/09_mpc_sentinel1_inventory.py`, the descending record over the bounding box of the blocks held `r format(s1_archive[["sentinel-1-grd"]], big.mark = ",")` Ground Range Detected scenes and `r format(s1_archive[["sentinel-1-rtc"]], big.mark = ",")` terrain corrected ones from 2017 to 2026, so the terrain correction cost `r sprintf("%.1f", s1_rtc_cost)` per cent of the scenes.

Two descending relative orbits, 131 and 160, crossed the blocks, and only orbit 131 entered the series, because it covered every block. Of the 160 blocks, `r s1_blocks[["only_131"]]` were seen by orbit 131 alone, `r s1_blocks[["both"]]` by both orbits and `r s1_blocks[["only_160"]]` by orbit 160 alone, so one track covered the whole sample and holding to it cost no block, where a series pooled across both would have given the `r s1_blocks[["both"]]` shared blocks a second viewing geometry the other `r s1_blocks[["only_131"]]` did not have. The two tracks view the same forest at different incidence angles, and on Earth Engine's unflattened sigma nought they had disagreed by about a decibel in K0 over the shared blocks, which is why the first design treated the track as a defect to be managed. The flattening removed it. On the terrain corrected record, over the `r s1_track[["n"]]` block-months both tracks observed, K0 on orbit 131 sat `r sprintf("%+.2f", s1_track[["mean"]])` dB from orbit 160 with a standard deviation of `r sprintf("%.2f", s1_track[["sd"]])` dB, so the offset between tracks was an artefact of the terrain and not of the forest, and orbit 160 was kept aside as an independent repeatability check on the blocks it shares. The published alternative was to normalise every observation to one fixed incidence angle, as the Sentinel-1 Global Backscatter Model does [@Bauer_Marschallinger_2021], which would admit the second track; it was not done because the collection's items carry no incidence angle field, so the angle would have to be rebuilt from the orbit geometry and the elevation model rather than read from the product. Figure S5 draws the two footprints over the blocks, which is the whole case for one track.

```{r}
#| label: tracks-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
fp_month <- with(s1_scenes, min(intersect(substr(date[track == 131], 1, 7),
                                          substr(date[track == 160], 1, 7))))
if (!file.exists("../03.outputs/s1_track_footprints.geojson")) {
  st_read(paste0(
    "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1/search?",
    "collections=sentinel-1-rtc&limit=200&bbox=",
    paste(round(st_bbox(st_transform(blocks, 4326)), 4), collapse = ","),
    "&datetime=", fp_month, "-01T00:00:00Z/", fp_month, "-28T23:59:59Z"
  ), quiet = TRUE) |>
    subset(sat.orbit_state == "descending",
           select = c(id, sat.relative_orbit, sat.orbit_state)) |>
    st_write("../03.outputs/s1_track_footprints.geojson", quiet = TRUE)
}
fp <- st_read("../03.outputs/s1_track_footprints.geojson", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(32605)
tracks <- aggregate(fp["id"], list(track = factor(fp$sat.relative_orbit)),
                    length) |>
  st_buffer(500) |>
  st_buffer(-500)
blocks$seen_by <- ifelse(sprintf("block_%03d", blocks$block) %in% seen[["160"]],
                         "Both tracks", "Track 131 only")
tracks_cap <- paste0(
  "Figure S5. Footprints of the two descending Sentinel-1 relative orbits that ",
  "cross the sampled blocks, 131 in green and 160 in violet, dissolved from the ",
  "scene outlines the Planetary Computer catalogue holds for ",
  format(as.Date(paste0(fp_month, "-01")), "%B %Y"), ", the first month both ",
  "orbits flew over the blocks. Filled squares are the ", s1_blocks[["both"]],
  " blocks both orbits see and hollow squares the ", s1_blocks[["only_131"]],
  " seen by orbit 131 alone, with ", s1_blocks[["only_160"]], " seen by orbit ",
  "160 alone. The dashed orange rectangle is the confirmatory study window. ",
  "WGS 84 UTM zone 5N (EPSG:32605), graticule in km."
)
```

```{r}
tm_shape(in_km(tracks), bbox = st_bbox(in_km(st_buffer(win_rect, 30000)))) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "track", col = "track", fill_alpha = 0.12, lwd = 0.8,
              fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = c("#1B9E77", "#7570B3")),

                col = "#E67E22", lty = "dashed", lwd = 0.7) +
```
